articles.title: Patrick Mahomes faces a potential Chiefs setback after Rashee Rice’s latest practice development
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes could be short of another key target when the Kansas City Chiefs return to action against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes could be short of another key target when the Kansas City Chiefs return to action against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday. Rashee Rice missed Wednesday’s practice with a hamstring injury, raising fresh questions about his availability for Week 6. The Chiefs are unbeaten at 4-0 and have had a bye to prepare, but Rice’s absence would complicate their plans. With Tyquan Thornton also out after suffering a serious ankle injury, Kansas City may have to rely more heavily on its younger receivers. That puts added pressure on Mahomes to adjust quickly if Rice cannot play.Rashee Rice’s practice absence creates another problem for Patrick MahomesRice has become an important part of Kansas City’s passing game, recording 13 catches for 190 yards and one touchdown in four games this season. His ability to find space and give Mahomes a dependable option makes his health a major concern, particularly with the Chiefs already missing Thornton.Rice injured his hamstring during the Week 4 game against the Las Vegas Raiders. Although the bye week gave him extra time to recover, he was still unable to practice on Wednesday. The Chiefs have not ruled him out for Sunday, but hamstring injuries can be difficult to predict. A player may feel better before he is ready to handle the demands of a full game.Head coach Andy Reid offered a cautious update on Rice’s condition.“We'll see how it goes,” Reid said of Rice's prospects for practicing later this week. “He's actually feeling pretty good as he goes here, so we'll see. Those things, you start dealing with hamstrings, and it could be a week, could be two weeks, you don't know, but I know he's eager to get back in.”Reid’s comments leave the door open for a return, but they also show why Kansas City cannot count on Rice just yet. The Chiefs will need to monitor his progress before deciding how much they can rely on him against the Chargers.Chiefs’ young receivers face a bigger test if Rice sits outRice’s potential absence also makes Thornton’s injury more significant. Kansas City has lost two receivers who could help stretch the field and create space for the rest of the offense. Xavier Worthy remains an option for Mahomes, but the Chiefs may also need Jalen Royals and Cyrus Allen to contribute more than they have so far.Mahomes has backed the younger players, pointing to their preparation and the trust they have built with him in practice.“They’ve put in the work,” Mahomes explained. “Obviously, we’ve had the guys in front of them with Tyquan going out there and playing great football, and so they’ve had to put in the work at practice, and they’ve been doing that. So now their number gets called, and they’re going to step into the role and do their job. I’m excited for them. We’ll put them in position to succeed. I have a lot of trust in those guys, a lot of confidence in them, and so we’ll continue to push it forward.”That trust will matter if the Chiefs have to change their plans on Sunday. Mahomes can help young receivers by keeping their assignments clear, but they must still read coverage, find openings and make plays when the ball comes their way.Kansas City has started well, yet Rice’s status is an important test of its depth. articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks have recorded an average run on the field in the new season as the team has won in 3 matches but lost in 2 so far.
articles.body: The Seattle Seahawks have recorded an average run on the field in the new season as the team has won in 3 matches but lost in 2 so far. In Weeks 1 and 2, the Seattle Seahawks ended up losing against the New England Patriots and the Arizona Cardinals but ended up losing in Week 3 against the Washington Commanders. articles.title: Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce reach major $3.69 million fundraising milestone as Team 62 delivers record-breaking autism support
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned a summer gathering into a powerful show of support for the autism community.
articles.body: Earlier this year, Jason Kelce and Kylie Kelce turned a summer gathering into a powerful show of support for the autism community. Their annual Team 62 fundraiser brought together Philadelphia Eagles fans, players, families and local supporters for a cause that continues to make a difference. The sixth edition raised more than $1.26 million in a single evening, pushing the event’s total fundraising past $3.69 million since 2021. Beyond the impressive figures, the achievement reflects how the couple have built a lasting connection with families affected by autism and helped strengthen the Eagles’ community outreach.Jason and Kylie Kelce push Team 62 fundraising past $3.69 millionThe latest Team 62 fundraiser took place on June 24 at Ocean Drive in Sea Isle City, New Jersey. What began as a charitable initiative has grown into a major annual event supporting the Eagles Autism Foundation, which funds autism research and community programmes.The record-breaking result also highlights the influence Jason and Kylie have built beyond football. Jason, a former Philadelphia Eagles centre and Super Bowl champion, remains a popular figure among fans. Alongside Kylie, he has helped make Team 62 a recurring opportunity for the community to support a cause that reaches far beyond the sport.The couple marked the milestone with gratitude for the people who have helped the fundraiser grow over six years.“Six years later, we now stand here amazed at what we’ve accomplished for the autism community,” read a statement.“A special thank you also goes out to the Eagles organization, the incredible town of Sea Isle City, and most importantly, the best fans in the world for always showing up and supporting such a worthy cause.”The continued growth of Team 62 shows how sustained community involvement can turn a local event into a significant fundraising effort.Team 62 brings the Eagles community together for autism supportThe fundraiser offered more than an evening of celebrity appearances. Organisers planned activities throughout the weekend to help people of different abilities participate and feel included.The Eagles Autism Foundation hosted an all-abilities football clinic, a cheerleading clinic, an Eagles drumline workshop, beach yoga and interactive activities for families. These sessions gave attendees opportunities to connect with the team and take part in the festivities.The main event at Ocean Drive featured celebrity bartenders from the current and former Eagles roster, members of the Kelce family, including Donna Kelce, team cheerleaders and mascot SWOOP. Guests could support the cause through tips, raffles, merchandise purchases and direct donations.Other fundraising efforts included the fourth annual Beer Bowl at the Sea Isle City Yacht Club, an online auction and entry fees from community activities.Eagles Autism Foundation executive director Ryan Hammond also praised Jason and Kylie for their commitment, recognising their role in making Team 62 one of the organisation’s key annual events.The $3.69 million milestone represents years of effort from the Kelces, the Eagles organisation and their supporters. With each edition bringing more people into the fold, Team 62 continues to show how sports, local partnerships and inclusive activities can help raise funds and awareness for the autism community.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: #AskTom: Which Team Would Tom Brady Most Want To Play For? Can Brock Purdy Win Super Bowl?
articles.summary: Tom Brady had a "simple answer" for which offense he'd most want to quarterback right now, and he's a believer in Brock Purdy.
articles.body: Rumors of Tom Brady's potential return to the gridiron have persisted since he last stepped off the gridiron at the end of the 2022 season. While he isn't planning a comeback, Brady knows exactly which team he would want to play for if he unretired today. In the latest edition of #AskTom, Brady had a "pretty simple" answer when asked which team he'd most want to play for. "I'm a veteran quarterback, and Matt Stafford's a veteran quarterback, too, playing for Sean McVay, playing with Puka [Nacua], playing with Davante [Adams], that three tight end grouping they run, Kyren Williams, Blake Corum (the Michigan Wolverine) and a damn good offensive line led by Ryan Wendell, my former center," Brady said, expressing a desire to quarterback the Los Angeles Rams in this hypothetical. Even though the Rams are off to a disappointing 2-3 start, their talent at the skill positions is undeniable. Nacua was named an All-Pro for the second time in his career last season and logged a career-high 17 catches in the Rams' Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills. Adams, meanwhile, is statistically having another strong season, ranking sixth in receiving yards (441) and is tied for fourth in receiving touchdowns (4). In fact, you could make the case that Stafford's play at quarterback could be hindering the Rams this season. While he leads the league in passing, Stafford's 88.3 passer rating is 21st in the league. As for Brady, he threw for 4,694 yards, 25 touchdowns and nine interceptions with a 90.7 passer rating as a 45-year-old in 2022. Would the now-49-year-old Brady be able to put up similar stats if he played for the Rams now? That we don't know. But we do know what Brady's thoughts are on Brock Purdy, as he praised the San Francisco 49ers' quarterback in the most recent edition of #AskTom. He also fielded questions from the MLB on FOX crew, with Derek Jeter, Alex Rodriguez and David Ortiz each asking for the GOAT's opinion on certain topics. Here's all of what Brady said in this week's #AskTom. Derek Jeter: I've been getting destroyed around here as of late, so I need an answer: Will our Wolverines bounce back? Brady: Listen, we're throwing the stats out. We are throwing the records out to this point — because they don't look very good right now. Look, I'm a Michigan Man. Derek, you're a Michigan Man. I'm riding with the Maize & Blue. We're gonna turn it around, and we're gonna be ready for those Buckeyes in November. Who's been the league's most impactful signing so far this season? Brady: I got a few. I just covered one in Seattle — he was the LFG Player of the Game: Mike Evans, my former teammate in Tampa, with over 100 yards against that defense. He's been lighting it up. He got some cracked ribs playing with the toughness that I knew when I played with him, and I'm glad he's on the national scene like he is right now. Also, don't forget about Nakobe Dean at the Raiders. What he's added at the middle linebacker position — so stout, so tough, some game-changing plays. That's another one. And, of course, you can't forget about this guy: K9, Kenneth Walker. He was leading the league in rushing through Week 4. He had a bye, but he's been off the chain this year. The way he's running, his physical toughness, his breakaway and the speed. He's been explosive, he's been efficient and he's been a catalyst for that Kansas City Chiefs offense. That was a hell of a signing for the Chiefs this offseason. Maybe you pick just one. Who is it? Brady: You're an a--hole, Kevin (laughs). I'm not picking one. I gave three for a reason. Can Brock Purdy lead his team to a Super Bowl if he needs to? Brady: He sure can. He's playing like one of the MVP favorites right now. He was leading the league in passer rating going into Seattle, distributing the ball to Evans, [George] Kittle and [Christian] McCaffrey, making plays on the move, extending plays on third down and scrambling when he needs to. He's making so many impact plays. So proud of him, the way that he's playing as a true field general out there, getting his team in the best place. He went up to Seattle and surprised a lot of people last Sunday. Way to go, Brock. Tom, you mentioned once that Brock was managing games so well, and I think some people took that as a shot, but that's not what you meant, right? Brady: Well, I think as a quarterback, you're always supposed to be managing every game. You're managing every situation. You're the coach on the field. You're the one that gets the last swipe of the pencil. You're the checks and balances of the whole offense, and when it's time to make a play out there, you do that too. You do what's easy, and when it requires, you do what's hard. Always get your team into the right play. And then sometimes, you gotta make something happen with your legs, and Brock's been able to do that. Alex Rodriguez: Where does our guy, Kevin Burkhardt, rank as far as your favorite Super Bowl teammates? Brady: Hey, two of my favorites on the Fox MLB desk. What a nice surprise. KB, A-Rod. You know what? It's hard to rank anyone at the top, but let me save this. KB, you are right at the top. I love being up there with you, partner. There's nobody I'd rather hang with on a Sunday. Let's do this for the rest of our lives. What do you say? Who are your favorite receivers in the league right now? Here's the caveat: JSN (Jaxon Smith-Njigba), J'Marr Chase, JJ (Justin Jefferson) and Puka Nacua are a given. We want your next four. Brady: I got Amon-Ra St. Brown from the Lions. He could easily be in that top tier group you mentioned. He does it all. He's a non-diva receiver too. He always finds a way inside, outside, run after catch. He does it all and blocks in the run game. Davante Adams, off to a hell of a year, a little throwback year from. The Rams weren't sure they were gonna bring him back this offseason, but he has proved them right being back in that uniform. He was great when Puka was out, still making those plays in the end zone. He's been ridiculous this year. CeeDee Lamb, he's been unbelievable. The Cowboys' offense — what they do in that dome, how they pass the ball — they're going to need that passing game to show up every week because the defense is struggling. The run game is struggling a little bit, but between Dak [Prescott], CeeDee and [George] Pickens, they'll get that passing game going and be a threat in the NFC East. And the last guy, I'm covering this Sunday in Atlanta for the very first time, Drake London. This is how you cut a promo right here. Drake London, I'm telling you, this guy is big, he's physical, he's fast and makes catches in traffic. He and Bijan [Robinson], I can't wait to see those guys lined up for the very first time in the dome. I'll be up there in Atlanta. Yeah, Atlanta, I know you're probably not excited to see me up there. Don't worry, I won't make too many 28-3 references. If Tom Brady had to step into one offense this season, with the goal of scoring the most possible points — so defense, head coach don't matter — who would it be? Where are you having the most fun? Brady: Well, that one's pretty simple, actually. I'm a veteran quarterback, and Matt Stafford's a veteran quarterback, too, playing for Sean McVay, playing with Puka, playing with Davante, that three tight end grouping they run, Kyren Williams, Blake Corum (the Michigan Wolverine) and a damn good offensive line led by Ryan Wendell, my former center. He and I still keep in touch, though. We still have a great relationship, not the same relationship I had when my hands were on his butt as a center with the New England Patriots for all those years, but we still have a great relationship. That's the offense I want to play for. You tell me you wouldn't fit in the Lamar Jackson, Derrick Henry RPO? Brady: You know, that is a little different for me. I think with my skinny legs and my lack of power and speed, that is not the appropriate offense for me to light up the scoreboard. What was the hardest defense that you ever went against schematically? Brady: So early in my career, we played the Miami Dolphins. It was a pretty simple coverage structure, a lot of two-high defense, ridiculous defensive ends, led by Jason Taylor. He was a menace in the run game and the pass game. At middle linebacker was Zach Thomas, another Hall of Famer, he tackled everybody and never missed a tackle. He was a ridiculous player in the run game, supported the entire back end of the defense in the pass game. Pat Surtain, Sam Madison — they could do it all. I think some of my worst career games came against those damn Dolphins defenses. I hated playing the Dolphins. They hemmed this up every time. We were lucky to get away with a few victories. Thank God we had a great defense, or we probably would have lost many more of those games. David Ortiz: Who is the Big Papi of the NFL? Brady: This one's easy. Head over to the "Gronk & Jules Show." Big Papi, it's "Gronk & Jules," two Boston legends, right there on the lot with me, just like you. We're all part of the FOX family. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: Who are Sam Darnold’s parents? Meet the plumber dad and PE teacher mom behind the Seahawks star’s rise
articles.summary: Sam Darnold’s path to the NFL has a family story that reaches beyond football.
articles.body: Sam Darnold’s path to the NFL has a family story that reaches beyond football. The Seattle Seahawks quarterback grew up with a father who worked as a plumber and a mother who taught physical education. Both parents brought their own connection to sports into his childhood, giving him a home where athletics were familiar but not the family’s only focus. His grandfather also had a notable sporting background, adding another layer to the family’s history. For fans curious about the person behind the quarterback, Mike and Chris Darnold offer a closer look at the people who shaped his early years.Who are Sam Darnold’s parents, Mike and Chris Darnold?Sam’s father, Mike Darnold, worked as a medical gas plumber, while his mother, Chris Darnold, built her career as a physical education teacher. Their professions were far removed from the demands and attention of professional football, but both had a clear connection to physical activity and sport.Chris’s work in physical education placed movement and fitness at the center of her professional life. Mike, meanwhile, worked outside the sports world. His job offered a different example for his son: a career built around practical skills and everyday responsibilities.That contrast makes the family’s story more interesting than a standard account of an NFL player’s upbringing. Sam grew up in a household where sport was part of the picture, but so was ordinary working life. His parents had careers of their own, and his development as an athlete took place alongside those commitments.The family did not need an NFL background to understand the value of sports. Their own experiences gave Sam a foundation before he began pursuing football at a higher level.How Sam Darnold’s family shaped his sporting backgroundAthletic ability runs through more than one branch of the Darnold family. Sam’s grandfather, Dick Hammer, was a former athlete who played basketball at the University of Southern California and competed in volleyball at the 1964 Summer Olympics. He later became known to television audiences for his role as the Marlboro Man.Hammer’s background gives Sam’s family history an unusual connection to both competitive sport and popular culture. His Olympic experience stands out, but the Marlboro Man association is another detail that may surprise football fans who know Sam mainly for his work as a quarterback.The family’s sporting history does not, by itself, explain Sam’s NFL career. Reaching the professional level takes years of training, performance and opportunity. Still, the presence of athletics across generations helps explain why sport was a familiar part of his family background.For Sam, that history offered a connection to competitive sport that stretched beyond his own football career. It also meant that his journey was not the first time someone in the family had pursued athletics at a high level.From a family home to the NFL spotlightSam’s rise has taken him into a world very different from the daily working lives of his parents. NFL quarterbacks face constant scrutiny, from their performances on Sundays to questions about their leadership and long-term prospects. Their families, however, often remain outside that public conversation.Mike and Chris Darnold’s backgrounds offer a more grounded view of Sam’s early life. One worked in plumbing, the other in education, and their family history included an Olympic athlete. Those details help explain the environment in which the quarterback grew up without reducing his success to his family connections.Sam’s career belongs to him, built through his own decisions and work on the field. But his story also has roots in a family whose experiences extended well beyond professional football. articles.body: Patrick Mahomes, the Kansas City Chiefs’ star player, and his wife, popular entrepreneur and investor Brittany Mahomes, have remained committed to their investment in the NWSL team, the Kansas City Current. As the Kansas City Current works on expanding the CPKC Stadium and building an entertainment district around it, there has been an update.Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ Kansas City Current makes the first move towards expansion around CPKC StadiumA few days ago, as per reports, there has been a launch of the first sports bar that has opened at Kansas City’s riverfront development, Current Landing. Revel, created by Shawn Lawson and Danney Elmore.The cafe is at the outdoor plaza just opposite to the entry to CPKC Stadium, home of the KC Current.In a press release, Josh Goldman, managing director at Palmer Square Real Estate, said, “The addition of Revel at Current Landing strengthens the district’s identity as a destination…It’s a social anchor—bringing together sophisticated hospitality, the energy of sport, and the rhythm of the riverfront into one cohesive experience.”Danney Elmore, the co-founder of the cafe, added, “We’re just happy to be down there at the Current Landing in the new entertainment district, and can’t wait to see what comes from it. articles.title: “Will help make that vision a reality”: How Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes’ foundation donates $15,000 to help children with autism as  their food allergy mission continues
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes' 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has donated $15,000 to the Thompson Foundation for Autism & Neurodevelopment to help build an accessible
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes' 15 and the Mahomies Foundation has donated $15,000 to the Thompson Foundation for Autism & Neurodevelopment to help build an accessible playground for children of all abilities. The grant will support the new Thompson Center at the University of Missouri, giving children a space to play and develop essential life skills.The donation is one part of the foundation's work with children and families. Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have also supported food allergy awareness through their partnership with Food Allergy Research & Education (FARE), a cause that became personal after their own children experienced allergic reactions. Patrick Mahomes' $15,000 grant will help create a playground for children of all abilitiesThe Thompson Foundation announced the grant on November 1, 2024. The playground is part of the new Thompson Center for Autism & Neurodevelopment and is designed to help children develop social, emotional, physical and mental skills through play.Dr. Connie Brooks, executive director of the Thompson Center, attended the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation Gala on October 28 with Jeremiah Oakley and his sister, Jakayla Henson. Brooks and Jeremiah accepted the donation from Mahomes at the event.Brooks explained how the playground could help children beyond their time outdoors.“The new playground will offer so much more than a place to play; it’s an environment where kids can practice important life skills in a setting designed specifically for them,” she said.She also thanked the foundation for supporting the project.“This grant from the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation will help make that vision a reality, and we’re excited to bring it to our community,” Brooks added.The new Thompson Center facility was designed to expand services for people with autism and other neurodevelopmental conditions. It will double the number of patient rooms, allowing the centre to care for more families. Patrick Mahomes and Brittany Mahomes continue supporting families dealing with food allergiesThe couple has also used their public platform to help families understand food allergies. Through their foundation's partnership with FARE, they have supported educational efforts aimed at helping parents prepare for allergic reactions and manage food allergies at home and school.Their involvement comes from personal experience. Brittany has spoken about the frightening reaction their son Bronze experienced as a baby after trying peanut powder. She noticed hives spreading across his body and face within minutes.Brittany already had an AUVI-Q epinephrine auto-injector because their daughter Sterling had previously experienced food allergies. She used the injector during Bronze's reaction, but the family still took him to the emergency room, where doctors monitored him for several hours.The family has since spoken publicly about the need for awareness and preparation. Their support for FARE has included fundraising and educational events for families navigating similar challenges.The Thompson Center grant focuses on a different need, but it reflects the foundation's wider work to support children and their families. In this case, the $15,000 contribution will help create a place where children of all abilities can play, learn and build social skills.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Tom Brady has spent years supporting Best Buddies International, a nonprofit that works with people with intellectual and developmental disabilities.
articles.body: Tom Brady has spent years supporting Best Buddies International, a nonprofit that works with people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. On Nov.17, 2023, the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback helped the organisation raise money through a golf experience that fetched $120,000 at its Miami gala.The auction offered more than a chance to play golf with an NFL legend. It supported a cause Brady had backed for over two decades, with the event raising $5 million in total for Best Buddies programs.How Tom Brady’s golf experience raised $120,000 for Best BuddiesAt the 25th Annual Best Buddies Miami Gala, Brady co-hosted a live auction with Anthony K. Shriver, the organisation’s founder, chairman and CEO. Their auction featured a golf experience and lunch at Indian Creek Golf Course. The package raised $120,000 for the nonprofit.Best Buddies announced the results on Nov. 22, 2023, in its official event report. The gala took place five days earlier and also honoured Brady with the Spirit of Leadership Award for his contributions to the organisation.The evening included a dinner, live and silent auctions, and a performance by Grammy-winning artist Nelly. Brady also tossed autographed footballs into the crowd as part of the fundraising effort.The golf auction formed one part of a larger event. Best Buddies said the gala raised $5 million to support its work creating opportunities for friendship, employment, leadership development and inclusive living for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Why Best Buddies has remained close to Tom BradyBrady’s involvement with Best Buddies goes well beyond one fundraising night. The organisation said he had served as a global ambassador, advocate and supporter for more than 20 years by November 2023. His work helped the nonprofit raise over $100 million.During his acceptance speech at the November 17, 2023, Miami gala, Brady spoke about the value of relationships and support systems.“There is nothing in our life that can be accomplished as an individual,” Brady said at the event. “It always comes down to who’s in our life, who’s supporting us and who our friends are. That’s what the Best Buddies mission is all about.”Best Buddies works to build friendships and create opportunities for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Its programs also support employment, leadership and independent living.Brady’s support for Best Buddies also reflects his belief in the role that friendship and strong personal connections play in people’s lives. His remarks at the gala went beyond the auction itself, highlighting the value of having people who offer support and encouragement. That message aligns with the organisation’s work to help people with intellectual and developmental disabilities build meaningful relationships and find greater opportunities in their communities.The gala showed how Brady used his public profile to help raise funds for that mission. articles.title: Broncos' offense goes nowhere after halftime but wins in OT after Seahawks' Sam Darnold throws INT
articles.summary: The Seahawks and Broncos had a defensive battle on Thursday night.
articles.body: DENVER — The 2025 Denver Broncos weren't always pretty, but they kept winning game after game until they finished with 14 W's in the regular season. The 2026 Broncos are taking that blueprint and running with it. The Broncos haven't been aesthetically pleasing through six games. They also have what is likely the best set of three quality wins of anyone in the NFL. They have beaten the Los Angeles Rams, Jacksonville Jaguars and on Thursday night they added the Seattle Seahawks to their list. Despite the Broncos' offense bogging down in the second half, which has been the case many times this season, the defense was excellent. It forced two interceptions against Sam Darnold, including one in overtime. Despite the repeated failures of the offense, which gained 30 yards in the third and fourth quarters, Denver found a way to win. Ja'Quan McMillian was the hero in overtime, picking off Darnold at Seattle's 43-yard line. Wil Lutz hit a 53-yard field goal to win it 17-14. Ja'Quan McMillian read this PERFECTLY. SEAvsDEN on Prime VideoStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/1igvuDtROG— NFL (@NFL) October 16, 2026 The Broncos are 4-2. Not everything has gone their way. The offense struggled so badly in the first four games that head coach Sean Payton took back play-calling duties from coordinator Davis Webb. And it hasn't been better with Payton calling plays. It's also tough to be too critical of a 4-2 team that has played one of the toughest schedules in the NFL, no matter how it has looked. The Broncos just keep winning ugly. Denver Broncos running back RJ Harvey, left, is lifted by teammate Quinn Meinerz (77) to celebrate Harvey's touchdown against the Seattle Seahawks.AP Photo/David ZalubowskiBroncos build strong first-half lead The Broncos had to figure out their offensive issues and do so against one of the NFL's best defenses. After a quick three-and-out, the Broncos went on what might be their best drive of the season.Picking up a pair of third-down conversions and one on fourth down, the Broncos drove 74 yards on 16 plays, and J.K. Dobbins finished it with a 4-yard touchdown run. There weren't a lot of explosive plays but it is hard to sustain a drive that long against Seattle, and Denver pulled it off. It seemed like a good sign for the Broncos. Then they followed it up with another nice drive, helped by a pass interference call in the end zone, and RJ Harvey scored on a 1-yard touchdown run. For a Broncos team that had struggled to move the ball over the first five games of the season, especially in the first half, a 14-3 lead at halftime was surprising.The good news for the Seahawks was the Broncos didn't score in the third and fourth quarters. Broncos' offense goes quiet in second half, Seahawks rally The Broncos weren't exactly moving it at will despite the 14-3 halftime lead. They had just 130 yards on offense in the first half. Then they gained 16 yards in the third quarter. But Seattle couldn't take advantage for three-plus quarters. The Seahawks couldn't sustain drives. Their run game lacked explosion, which has been a theme all season. The passing game didn't do much either. But the Broncos' defense was a big part of that. Their pass rush in particular was a big reason Sam Darnold couldn't find anyone downfield. He was sacked five times Thursday night. But finally in the fourth quarter the Seahawks found the end zone. They got a fourth-down conversion to Jaxon Smith-Njigba and that led to a touchdown run by George Holani and a juggling 2-point conversion catch by Rashid Shaheed. The Broncos' offense had done almost nothing in the second half when it suddenly found itself needing to protect a 14-11 lead. Bo Nix got sacked, a run play gained little and then Nix took another sack for a quick three-and-out. Darnold hit Smith-Njigba for a 32-yard gain on a great contested catch over the middle, getting Seattle on the verge of field-goal range. But Darnold rushed a pass that was picked off by Kris Abrams-Draine, turning away the threat. That seemed like it would seal the win. But Nix and company did nothing after that, with another quick three-and-out. Seattle had one more shot with 57 seconds left after a long Shaheed punt return got the Seahawks to their own 46-yard line. A few passes got them comfortably into field-goal range, and with three seconds left Jason Myers tied it to send the game to overtime. In overtime, Darnold made another critical mistake, throwing a pick to Ja'Quan McMillan. That was all the Broncos needed to get Lutz the field goal and escape with a win.

articles.title: Seattle, Sam Darnold Are Struggling: 3 Takeaways From Broncos' OT Win vs. Seahawks
articles.summary: Sam Darnold's woes have continued. Here are three takeaways from the Broncos' overtime win over the Seahawks.
articles.body: In a game that looked like a 1980s flashback with the Seattle Seahawks and Denver Broncos wearing their throwback uniforms from their AFC West rivalry days, the defending Super Bowl champs appear to have lost their swagger. The Broncos took a double-digit lead into halftime, but needed overtime to escape with a 17-14 victory over the visiting Seahawks in primetime on Thursday night. The victory upped Denver’s record to 4-2 on the year and improved their home record to 17-3 since the start of the 2024 season, while Seattle dropped to the .500 mark at 3-3 for the first time this season. The reeling Seahawks have lost three of their last four games. The Broncos remain fortunate in close games. All four of Denver's wins this season have come by seven points or fewer, and dating back to last season, the Broncos have won their last 14 regular-season games decided by a single score. Here are my takeaways. 1.Sam Darnold Can’t Shake The Funk Since returning from a glute injury, Darnold’s struggles have continued for Seattle. He finished 27 of 51 for 278 yards, with no touchdown passes and two interceptions — and both picks came at a bad time. The first one was on a bad throw that stopped a potential scoring drive in the final minutes of the fourth quarter and the second one came in overtime, which sealed Seattle’s fate. Darnold now has seven interceptions this season, and he was under duress most of the night by Denver’s defense and didn’t make many plays down the field. Darnold was sacked five times and struggled to handle Denver’s pressure. Darnold finished 6 of 19 for 47 yards and two interceptions when pressured by the Broncos’ defensive front, according to Next Gen Stats. It’s fair to wonder if the Seahawks might consider a change to Drew Lock at quarterback, who played well while Darnold was injured. With Broncos standout defensive backs Patrick Surtain II and Talanoa Hufanga unavailable because of injury, Denver slowed down Seattle’s No. 1 target Jaxon Smith-Njigba early. However, the reigning Offensive Player of the Year exploded late, finishing with 12 receptions for 134 yards. Entering Thursday’s contest, Smith-Njigba led the NFL with 583 receiving yards and seven touchdowns. 2.Bo Nix Looks A Little More Comfortable, But Still Not Playing Well Enough Broncos head coach Sean Payton, who was serving in his second game as Denver’s offensive playcaller since taking back that role from offensive coordinator Davis Webb, had Nix playing with his most confidence this season, at least in the opening portion of Thursday's game. The Broncos leaned on the running game to take pressure off Nix, which created easy completions for the Oregon product. Nix was an efficient 17-of-27, but that led to just 107 yards without a touchdown or interception. Payton schemed up quick throws for Nix, who was sacked twice and rarely felt pressure from one of the best defenses in the NFL. However, that momentum from the first half failed to carry into the second half. Denver couldn't close out the game, totaling just 30 yards and six punts in the second half. It went three-and-out ahead of four of those punts, allowing Seattle to get back into the game despite its offensive woes all night long. 3.Seattle's Darkside Defense Rebounds After Slow Start Speaking of that Seattle defense, the Seahawks are off their game defensively to start the year. Seattle allowed 30 or more points just twice last season. However, the Seahawks have given up at least 30 points in two of their last three games and allowed a Denver offense that had been struggling to establish control of the game early by taking a 14-3 lead into halftime. Specifically, Seattle’s usually stout defense allowed the Broncos to march down the field on two touchdown drives that went for a combined total of 153 yards on 25 plays. The Broncos' ability to run the football against the Seahawks allowed Nix to play from a comfortable pocket most of the game, and Seattle got little pressure on Denver's quarterback, who was pressured on just 20% of his dropbacks (He finished 0-for-4 on those throws). But the Seahawks' defense had a stronger showing in the second half. As we mentioned earlier, the Broncos only had 30 yards in the final 30 minutes, as the Seahawks' defense gave their team a chance to win the game.

articles.title: What do NFL evaluators really see in Arch Manning's uneven season? 'There's a lot more polished guys that are farther along'
articles.summary: Arch Manning was the presumptive QB1 prospect for the 2027 NFL Draft, but he hasn't yet ironed out his inconsistencies. What does this mean for his stock?
articles.body:
Two fourth-quarter throws helped end Texas' perfect season last Saturday against Oklahoma . They also raised questions about the most famous QB prospect in college football.

First came Arch Manning's pick-6 with 10:07 remaining, giving Oklahoma the lead. Then, after Texas tied it, Manning's second pick in the final 30 seconds set up the Sooners' game-winning field goal in a 27-24 shocker.

Manning had some brilliant moments in the first three quarters of the Red River Rivalry, including two high-level touchdown throws, and he added another terrific TD pass between the two interceptions. But the two turnovers proved decisive in the loss.

It was a near-perfect encapsulation of Arch, the NFL prospect: brilliant mixed with maddening.

"Bad decision, bad mechanics, bad throw," an AFC scouting director said of the pick-6. "But he did some good things in that game. Really good. That's where you're kind of stuck as an evaluator. Like, how do I judge this?"

Blessed with NFL-caliber skills and QB-royalty bloodlines, Manning entered this season as the presumptive top QB prospect in what has been touted as a potentially great 2027 NFL Draft class at the position. But an uneven start to his 2026 season has NFL talent evaluators questioning what they're seeing — and whether Manning has made the kind of progress expected from a provisional No. 1 overall draft pick.

Two evaluators we spoke to were ambivalent about Manning as a prospect right now. Both see some of the same symptoms — late reads, not enough on-time throws, poor ball placement — and agree that the product has been slightly disappointing to this point, even if hope in Manning remains relatively high.

"He's athletic. He has the tools, but it's still coming together," one senior NFC evaluator said. "... Right now he's not ready, just as a complete prospect, of reading coverages, making good decisions and delivering accurate balls on a consistent basis. It's just not there. ... It's coming. You see the glimpses. He's tough. He's competitive. He uses his legs."

The quarterback hierarchy for the 2027 draft is far from set in stone. But Manning's perceived grip on the top spot has significantly loosened, especially as, on balance, Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker, Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss and Miami's Darian Mensah have authored arguably more impressive tape this season and prospects such as Notre Dame's CJ Carr and Missouri's Austin Simmons have made big moves from the start of the season.

"I think we tend to rush [Manning's] development just because of his last name," the NFC evaluator said. "... I don't think it's there yet. There's a lot more polished guys that are farther along than he is."

Can Manning reestablish his draft standing with a strong finish like he had in 2025? Are his mistakes fixable? And could he even return to college next season? All those questions hang in the air as Manning and Texas enter a crucial stage of their season.

Manning, the grandson of former Saints legend Archie Manning and the nephew of Peyton and Eli Manning, had greatness projected on him before he ever set foot in Texas. But after nearly four years of college, starting for the past two seasons, his picture remains incomplete.

This was supposed to be Manning's breakthrough season. The surge began in the second half of the 2025 season, when he played some of the best ball of his college career. In Texas' final six games, Manning threw for 1,714 yards, 14 TDs and two interceptions, ran for 206 yards and five more scores and even caught a TD pass.

Texas added wideout Cam Coleman, offensive tackle Melvin Siani and running backs Raleek Brown and Hollywood Smothers, and retained a host of blue-chip talent, including future first-rounders such as OT Trevor Goosby and WR Ryan Wingo. Even in the rough-and-tumble SEC, with Texas facing arguably the nation's toughest schedule, greatness was the expectation.

That hasn't quite happened yet. Manning and Texas have yet to reach their peaks, even with a shocking 20-point comeback over then-No. 1 Ohio State in Week 2. In that game, Manning pulled off the stunner with three TD drives in the fourth quarter. Even that outing came with its warts.

"I didn't think he was that good [against OSU]," the AFC director said. "He helped them win for sure, but he had plays to make that he just flat-out missed. They were very lucky to win that one."

Three up-and-down games later, including the fourth-quarter mistakes against Oklahoma, Manning feels like he's in the same place he was before the hot finish last season. The high-end throws are highly enticing. The critical errors are a serious deterrent. Manning remains a complicated prospect.

'Flawed' doesn't spell doom in the draft

Then again, several flawed prospects have ended up being drafted very high in recent years. Blake Bortles (2014, No. 3), Josh Allen (2018, No. 7), Daniel Jones (2019, No. 6) and Zach Wilson (2021, No. 2) are examples of prospects who, regardless of how their NFL careers have turned out, landed in the top 10 while facing questions about accuracy, mechanics and decision-making.

In a traits-over-production league, there are still enough positive elements to Manning's game that could keep him close to the top of the draft. There is also the desperation factor.

"Every year there's more quarterback-needy teams than there are early [QB prospects]," the NFC evaluator said. "That's where you get the fourth guy [in Round 1], you know? Where he's really the sixth or seventh guy, but he's the fourth guy for this year. ...

"We sometimes grasp for salvation at that position."

Neither evaluator was willing to reveal exactly where they'd slot Manning in this class given how relatively early it is in the draft process.

"You don't always have the answers," the senior NFC talent evaluator said. "Middle of October, you're finding out what it is and what are the questions that need to be asked."

An echo of his play in the back half of 2025 could vault Manning back up toward the top of the class. But what if his season continues on the current trajectory or slides even further down?

"I can see the kid coming back," the NFC evaluator said. "You know, you're talking about wise counsel [in the Manning family]. I think he's going to make a good decision regardless. … It'll be interesting."

Because of his pedigree and impressive physical qualities, most Manning comps start with big names. Yet the scouting director found a more apples-to-apples comparison farther down the food chain.

"Trevor was more polished," the AFC director said.

"Closer, but not exactly who I thought."

"I see Daniel Jones. Daniel Jones is a pretty good quarterback, now. Arch is, too. But style-wise, and just the questions that come into my head when I watch him, it's like the Daniel Jones experience all over again: big, talented, athletic kid … decision-making questionable, [inconsistent] ball placement. That's what I've seen so far."

Both evaluators agree that getting to the root of Manning's unsteadiness is the key to unlocking him as a prospect.

"It's not only tape; it's going through and getting an understanding of the whys behind it," the NFC evaluator said. "... That's part of the deep dive."

The biggest word that comes up with Manning? Consistency.

"More tools-traits prospect than complete player, to me, right now," the AFC director said. "He's at, what, 20 or so starts? But it's been four years in the same system. … You'd like to see more development by this stage."

The director has attended one of Manning's games in person this season and seen most of the tape from his five games. Even while noting that Texas' issues are far from all being on Manning, there have still been too many issues cropping up on his tape — even on successful plays.

"It just looks like he's not seeing the field that great," the AFC director added. "Extra hitches when they're not needed. Getting hung up on [his first reads]. Turning down open throws. Late on some stuff, even completions. Ball placement, not always great. Sacks that shouldn't be sacks. … He's leaving some meat on that bone, and I'd like to see it picked cleaner."

The other issue seems to be game feel: knowing when to press and when to be smart. That was on display in the Oklahoma loss, but it's also shown up in other games.

"It's him risk-taking when you want the checkdown, and it's a checkdown when you want him taking chances," the director said. "It's backward to me. I'd like to know what he's thinking on some of these throws, or what he's been taught. Because some of it doesn't make sense."

Manning has seven games left in the regular season, with his draft stock and Texas' season hanging in the balance. The Longhorns' next three games are in Austin, starting with a Florida team that flummoxed Manning in 2025, followed by tough home games against No. 9 Ole Miss and No. 16 Mississippi State. After a couple more difficult road games at No. 13 Missouri and No. 22 LSU, Texas finishes at home with current SEC bottom dwellers Arkansas and Texas A&M.

This stretch will determine whether Manning and Texas can fulfill their lofty expectations. Both evaluators agree that the potential is there for both quarterback and team to finish on high notes. The talent is there. The bulk of the season remains in front of them. But one way or another, for Manning to reach his ceiling, he's going to have to beat the clock — both in the pocket and in his head.

"We just gotta play more on time, man," the AFC director said.

articles.title: Sam Darnold takes responsibility for Seahawks' loss at Denver: 'It's BS for me to keep turning the ball over'
articles.summary: The Seahawks fell 17-14 in overtime after Darnold's second interception of the game.
articles.body:
DENVER — Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold didn't wait for a question when he met the media after Thursday night's loss. It's not like he didn't know what was coming.

"No way to sugarcoat it, that one sucked," said Darnold, who threw two late interceptions in a 17-14 defeat to the Denver Broncos , including a crucial one in overtime. "Can't turn the ball over, obviously that's at the forefront of my mind."

He was just as blunt with his teammates afterward. He took responsibility for the interceptions. He was asked afterward why he felt the need to address the team.

"I just think it's BS for me to keep turning the ball over," Darnold said. "It's not fair to our defense, it's not fair to our special teams group, not fair really to the entire team. I've got to be better that way."

Last season, Darnold redefined his career by helping Seattle win a Super Bowl. But he didn't kick his turnover habit, at least in the regular season. He had 14 interceptions and a league-high 11 fumbles, losing six. Magically, he didn't turn the ball over last postseason. But this season he has seven interceptions despite playing only four full games. It was costly Thursday night.

The Seahawks held the Broncos to 38 offensive yards in the second half and overtime. Their special teams made plays, including a long punt return late in regulation that set up a game-tying field goal. Darnold's turnovers weren't the only reason Seattle lost, and the other Seahawks pointed that out repeatedly. But the Seahawks are 3-3, with three losses in close games, and a big reason is Darnold is making too many big mistakes.

"We have to take care of the ball," Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said. "Sam knows that, he told the team that. Gotta take care of the ball."

Sam Darnold 'got greedy' on interception in OT

Darnold's first interception seemed like it would end the game. He was pressured and hurried a pass that was picked off by Broncos cornerback Kris Abrams-Draine at Denver's 31-yard line with Seattle trailing 14-11 and 1:31 left in regulation.

But the Seahawks' defense came through, forcing a quick three-and-out. Seattle drove in the final minute and tied it to send the game to overtime. The Seahawks got the ball first and Darnold tried to force a pass into Cover 2, but it was played well by cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian and picked off at Seattle's 43-yard line. The Broncos gained 8 yards, kicked a field goal and escaped with the win. He said he should have hit Cooper Kupp underneath for what he thought would have been a first down.

While Darnold took responsibility for the turnovers, others pointed out several issues within the offense. Macdonald said multiple times that "our quarterback got hit too much today." Denver registered 17 quarterback hits and had five sacks. The lack of a run game has been an issue most of the season for a Seahawks team that let Kenneth Walker III leave in free agency, though Seattle had a reasonable 113 rushing yards Thursday night. There's an over-reliance on star wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the passing game.

It all puts a lot of pressure on Darnold, and that's not good for a quarterback who has had turnover issues his entire career.

"A lot is going to be put on Sam for the result at the end of the day, but we're all out there with him and we all have a responsibility," Kupp said. "We all play a role in protecting the football. He's going to own that, because that's who he is, but we're not going a good enough job offensively to allow him to play in rhythm, we're not doing a good enough job allowing him to get into a flow, turning small plays into big plays, not doing a good enough job in the run game, not doing a good enough job protecting him. There's a lot of things that need to improve."

Seahawks already match last season's loss total

This season's Seahawks will be constantly compared to last season's title team. It happens to every reigning champion, especially if they struggle. Last season was a tremendous year from a dominant champion that lost only three games. They've lost three games already this season.

It's hard to duplicate any season as dominant as the one the 2025 Seahawks had. Losing Walker, and also running back Zach Charbonnet who hasn't played yet after tearing his ACL in the playoffs, has affected the offense. Everything with that unit looks more difficult. On Thursday night, Seattle had just three points until its first touchdown with 5:41 to go in the fourth quarter.

"I'm not going to compare last year and this year. This is the 2026 Seahawks," Darnold said. "There's a lot of things we need to get better at and I'll leave it at that."

The Seahawks are 3-3 and while the frustration is evident, they also talked about how they battled Thursday night to take the game to overtime, and how they've been close in all three losses. The three losses have come by a combined eight points.

"I feel like we're doing well, we're showing what type of team we are at times, but we're not doing enough to close out these games that we should be," Seahawks defensive lineman Leonard Williams said.

Macdonald talked about Seattle's advantage of playing complementary football through all three phases, and part of that is not just the quarterback's play but running the ball and protecting him better. But it also has to include Darnold not turning it over at a startling pace.

"It wasn't a performance that was good enough to win the game. By our team. But the quarterback leads the team," Macdonald said. "I bet Sam would be the first one to tell you that."

articles.title: In 2024, Dak Prescott signed a $240 million Cowboys contract with $231 million guaranteed
articles.summary: Dak Prescott secured his place at the centre of the Dallas Cowboys' future in September 2024, when he signed a record-breaking contract extension worth
articles.body: Dak Prescott secured his place at the centre of the Dallas Cowboys' future in September 2024, when he signed a record-breaking contract extension worth $240 million. The four-year agreement included $231 million in guaranteed money and an $80 million signing bonus, making him the NFL's highest-paid player by average annual value at the time. The deal came just hours before Dallas opened its season against the Cleveland Browns. For Prescott, it was a major financial milestone. For owner Jerry Jones, it was a costly commitment to a quarterback expected to lead one of football's most valuable franchises towards another Super Bowl.How Dak Prescott secured his $240 million Cowboys contractThe agreement arrived after months of uncertainty over Prescott's future in Dallas. Entering the 2024 season, the quarterback was in the final year of his previous four-year, $160 million contract. Without an extension, he could have entered free agency in 2025, leaving the Cowboys facing the possibility of losing their starting quarterback without receiving anything in return.Both sides had strong reasons to reach an agreement. Prescott wanted long-term security, while Dallas needed stability at the most important position in football. Negotiations continued into the opening weekend before the team announced the deal on September 8, 2024.Prescott was preparing for the season opener when his agent, Todd France, delivered the news. ESPN reported that the quarterback was in his hotel room in Cleveland with teammate Ezekiel Elliott and his physical therapist when the call came through.The agreement gave Prescott a four-year extension worth $240 million, keeping him under contract through the 2028 season. It also raised the financial stakes for a franchise that had struggled to turn regular-season success into deep playoff runs.Prescott expressed his desire to remain with Dallas rather than pursue another team.“I wanted to be a Cowboy,” he said. “I wanted to stay a Cowboy and it got done.”The statement reflected his connection to the organisation, which selected him in the fourth round of the 2016 NFL Draft. Since then, he had developed into one of the league's leading quarterbacks and a central figure in the Cowboys' offence.According to NFL.com, the extension included $231 million in guaranteed money and an $80 million signing bonus. citeturn797939search0Breaking down Dak Prescott's $231 million guaranteed contractThe headline figure attracted attention across the NFL, but the contract's structure matters just as much as its total value.Prescott's $240 million agreement averages $60 million per season. That figure made him the first NFL player to reach a $60 million average annual value, setting a new benchmark for quarterback pay at the time.The contract also included $231 million in total guarantees. However, total guaranteed money and money fully guaranteed at signing are not the same thing. Reports placed the amount fully guaranteed at signing at $129 million, with additional guarantees tied to future contract conditions.The deal's key financial details were:Total contract value: $240 million over four years.Total guaranteed money: $231 million.Fully guaranteed at signing: $129 million, according to ESPN's contract reporting.Signing bonus: $80 million.Average annual value: $60 million.Contract length: Through the 2028 NFL season.The $80 million signing bonus provided Prescott with a substantial payment at the start of the agreement. Meanwhile, the salary and guarantee structure gave both sides a framework for managing the contract over several seasons.Dallas also secured protections within the deal, including reported no-trade and no-franchise-tag provisions. Those terms limited some of the team's options while giving Prescott greater control over his future.The agreement surpassed the previous benchmark set by Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson, whose contract included $230 million fully guaranteed. Prescott's $231 million in total guarantees therefore set a new record for the largest guaranteed amount reported in an NFL contract at the time.ESPN's report covered Prescott's reaction to the deal and his motivation to turn the financial milestone into success on the field. citeturn797939search1Why the Dallas Cowboys invested so heavily in Dak PrescottPrescott's contract reflected more than his passing statistics. Dallas had built its offence around him, and replacing an established starting quarterback would have created a major challenge for the organisation.His 2023 season offered a strong case for the investment. Prescott threw for 4,516 yards and 36 touchdowns, with nine interceptions. He also finished second in the NFL Most Valuable Player voting, reinforcing his standing among the league's top quarterbacks.The Cowboys entered the 2024 campaign after winning 12 regular-season games in each of the previous three seasons. Prescott had helped guide Dallas to the playoffs in those years, making him an important part of the team's consistent regular-season success.However, his playoff record remained a concern. Dallas had not reached the Super Bowl since the 1995 season, and Prescott had yet to lead the franchise to the championship game.That history added pressure to the new agreement. A large contract can secure a player's future, but it cannot guarantee postseason success. Prescott and the Cowboys now had an even greater financial commitment tied to the same goal.The quarterback's new deal also arrived after Dallas had extended wide receiver CeeDee Lamb on a four-year contract worth approximately $136 million. Keeping both players gave the Cowboys an established passing combination, although it also required the team to manage a significant portion of its salary cap around offensive talent.The decision showed how much Dallas valued continuity. Yet it also meant the organisation would face continued scrutiny over its ability to build a complete roster around its highly paid stars.Dak Prescott's $240 million deal puts Super Bowl expectations in focusPrescott's contract extension settled one major question about his future, but it did not settle the debate over his legacy.At the time of signing, the deal placed him at the top of the NFL's pay scale. That status brought recognition, security and a clear message about the Cowboys' faith in him. It also raised expectations for what he needed to deliver.For Dallas, the challenge is to turn its investment into postseason progress. A quarterback earning $60 million annually is expected to lead an offence capable of competing with the strongest teams in the league. That requires more than individual production. Protection from the offensive line, reliable receivers, a balanced running game and a strong defence all play a role.Prescott's extension also illustrates how quickly the NFL's financial landscape changes. Quarterback contracts continue to rise as teams compete to secure elite players, and a record deal can become an ordinary benchmark within a few seasons.Still, the numbers tell only part of the story. Prescott had spent his entire professional career with Dallas, developing from a fourth-round selection into the franchise's long-term starter. The 2024 agreement rewarded that progress and removed the immediate threat of free agency.The ultimate test, however, remains the same.
