articles.title: Best and Worst Landing Spots for WRs Potentially Available at 2026 NFL Trade Deadline
articles.summary: The NFL trade deadline looms, but we have already seen one major deal involving a big-name wide receiver—Marvin Harrison Jr., the No. 4 overall pick in 2024, will try to jump-start his career in Houston after the Arizona Cardinals dealt him to the Texans.
articles.body:
The NFL trade deadline looms, but we have already seen one major deal involving a big-name wide receiver—Marvin Harrison Jr., the No. 4 overall pick in 2024, will try to jump-start his career in Houston after the Arizona Cardinals dealt him to the Texans.

It's possible we aren't done at the position. There are a handful of prominent wideouts who have been mentioned of late in trade talks. Some, like Harrison, were once first-round picks. More than one has a 1,000-yard season on their professional resume. Others only recently signed with new teams, but those partnerships already appear to be poor fits.

Midseason deals for veteran receivers often involve contenders, although Houston's acquisition of Harrison shows that isn't always the case.

However, a team's need for a receiver doesn't necessarily make it the right fit. For each of those wideouts who could be on the move, there's an ideal potential landing spot.

As a rookie in 2024, Brian Thomas Jr. was outstanding—he reeled in 87 passes for 1,282 yards and 10 touchdowns. But he missed three games last year and saw his production drop considerably, and hopes for a rebound season in 2026 haven't come to pass.

In fact, Thomas has fallen behind both Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers in the wideout pecking order in Jacksonville, and he has played a 60 percent snap share just once in five games this season.

The 49ers continue winning despite being hit by new injuries each and every week, and the wide receiver room hasn't been spared—Deebo Samuel Sr. suffered a hamstring injury last week that is expected to cost him multiple games. Mike Evans has also been battling a rib injury.

In San Francisco, Thomas wouldn't be expected to carry the wide receiver room. But with Evans and (eventually) Samuel drawing coverage away, he should also be able to get open with regularity.

Evans and Thomas outside and Samuel in the slot isn't a bad trio at all. Add tight end George Kittle to that mix, and Brock Purdy would have quite the array of weaponry at his disposal.

Worst Landing Spot: New England Patriots

Despite being without A.J. Brown for most of the season, the Patriots have shaken off a 1-2 start with back-to-back impressive wins. But the team could use an upgrade at the No. 2 wideout spot opposite Brown.

This just isn't an ideal landing spot for Thomas to command a large target share. Brown figures to draw a substantial portion of the targets once he returns. And while there aren't any other big names in the Patriots' passing game, Drake Maye has still been spreading the ball around.

Thomas could find himself in the same situation in Beantown as in Duval County—a secondary option who doesn't receive consistent targets.

The Baltimore Ravens are a contender in their own right, so it might appear odd that the team would trade away their No. 2 wide receiver.

But per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , Bateman's name continues to be mentioned in trade discussions ahead of the deadline:

"Another player I'm keeping an eye on is Baltimore's Rashod Bateman. Zay Flowers is the dominant wide receiver in the Ravens' offense, which means Bateman's production comes and goes. Bateman's contract is tradable—he is due $6.5 million this year and $8.25 million in 2027—and other teams have had interest in the past. The Ravens are in contention and might not want to move players, but Bateman is at least a name on my list."

We know one thing: Rams general manager Les Snead isn't averse to making deals for veteran players. Despite a 2-3 start, the Rams remain committed to contending.

In Los Angeles, Bateman could slide even farther down the depth chart. But he could be highly valuable to the Rams if the injury bug gets Puka Nacua again. He'd also be a move for the future—Davante Adams isn't getting any younger, and Bateman's 2027 salary is reasonable.

The Colts have been mentioned as a potential landing spot for just about every wideout who might be available. With Alec Pierce out indefinitely with a foot injury, the team badly needs to add some pop to the passing attack.

The problem for Bateman in Indianapolis would be twofold. First, there are questions about Daniel Jones' effectiveness following last year's Achilles tear. Second, the Colts already have multiple complementary receivers.

If they trade for a wideout, they need a clear-cut No. 1 rather than another complementary receiver like Bateman.

Not that long ago, Jerry Jeudy was the No. 1 wide receiver for the Cleveland Browns. He caught 90 passes for 1,229 yards and made the Pro Bowl with the team in 2024.

Now, Jeudy has largely disappeared from Cleveland's passing attack. He has been passed by rookie KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston on the depth chart and has just eight catches for 81 yards for the season.

That reduced role has led to rampant trade speculation. As Andrew Hughes of Athlon Sports noted, Jeudy's contract could appeal quite a bit to potential suitors.

"Jeudy carries a $9.175 million cap hit this season, and the nearly $23 million he is due in 2027 is not guaranteed, according to his Spotrac page . A contender could rent him for half a season and walk away in March. The catch for Cleveland is that a trade would leave more dead money than his 2026 cap hit."

The New York Giants didn't expect to necessarily be contenders this season, especially after quarterback Jaxson Dart was lost for the season. But at 3-1-1, they hold a 1.5-game lead atop the NFC East.

The Giants could use an upgrade at their second receiver spot over Darnell Mooney, and Jeudy has familiarity with current Giants quarterback Jameis Winston—Winston started seven games for the Browns in 2024, and he and Jeudy had a strong rapport over that stretch.

Miami looks unlikely to contend for a playoff spot, but it could still add a veteran receiver to help evaluate Malik Willis.

Joining a struggling offense could make it harder for Jeudy to rebuild his value, potentially leaving him seeking a one-year "prove it" deal if Miami moves on next offseason.

Quentin Johnston's inconsistency reflects the Chargers' broader struggles in 2026.

When the 25-year-old was drafted 21st overall by the Chargers in 2023, he was expected to anchor the passing attack for years to come. Instead, he has struggled with consistency, has yet to reach 750 receiving yards in a season and has seven catches this year.

As G.C. Bellchamber wrote for Bolt Beat , the Chargers have also already picked up Johnston's fifth-year option, which makes trading him that much more problematic.

"Any team that would be willing to take a swing on him would be betting not only on his upside within its offense—it would be betting on his ability to justify the $16.5 million salary he's already owed for next season," Bellchamber said.

To be clear, this is exceedingly unlikely. The Chiefs aren't dropping $16.5 million next year on Johnston, and the Chargers would be reluctant to trade him to an AFC West rival.

But Johnston would fill a clear need for the team. He's a one-for-one replacement for the injured Tyquan Thornton: a vertical threat who could occasionally take the top off opposing defenses.

Green Bay has been mentioned as a potential landing spot for Johnston, and the argument can be made that with Jayden Reed sidelined, the Packers could use another body at the position.

But they already have a big-bodied burner on the roster in No. 1 wide receiver Christian Watson, and it wouldn't be good for Johnston or Green Bay for him to slot in as the fourth option in the passing game behind Watson, Matthew Golden and tight end Tucker Kraft.

The Minnesota Vikings signed Jauan Jennings in the offseason to a one-year, $8 million contract worth up to $13 million with incentives, bringing him in as a complementary piece alongside superstar Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

The Vikings were going to have one of the most formidable wideout trios in the league.

Instead, Jennings has had a minimal role, catching two passes for nine yards in total.

With the 29-year-old struggling to establish a role, the Vikings could consider moving on before his one-year contract expires, as Carter Bahns of CBS Sports noted:

"There appears to be a lack of chemistry between Jennings and his quarterbacks, and he is clearly a far worse fit in Kevin O'Connell's offense than that of Kyle Shanahan. For those reasons, and because he can leave of his own volition at the end of the season, the Vikings could work toward a trade over the next month."

The Raiders have been surprisingly competitive this season, but the team has one of the weakest assemblages of wide receiver talent in the NFL. At some point, Fernando Mendoza is going to start at quarterback, and when he does it would be nice to have a reliable target not named Brock Bowers.

More importantly, the Raiders are coached by Klint Kubiak, who runs a variation of Shanahan's West Coast offense. The team is a far better scheme fit for what Jennings does well, and he could be acquired for a mid-to-late Day 3 pick.

The Steelers could use another wide receiver. The Michael Pittman Jr. trade has yet to produce the expected results, and Roman Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks with a hand injury. Mike McCarthy's West Coast offense isn't a bad fit for Jennings either.

But Jennings would need time to build a rapport with Aaron Rodgers, potentially limiting his immediate role.

Were Jennings to land in Pittsburgh, he could wind up in the same situation as in the Twin Cities: an afterthought in the offense.

articles.title: Predicting When Vulnerable Starting NFL Quarterbacks Get Benched
articles.summary: For various reasons, about a quarter of the NFL's starting quarterbacks could be at risk of losing their jobs.
articles.body:
For various reasons, about a quarter of the NFL's starting quarterbacks could be at risk of losing their jobs.

Some are struggling individually, while others could give way to younger backups amid mounting outside pressure or team-wide struggles.

Here's how I see each scenario playing out.

The Problem: The Cardinals have lost four consecutive games, with the 33-year-old Brissett posting an ugly 81.1 passer rating during that time frame. Brissett threw three interceptions in a Week 4 loss to the Giants and was sacked five times in a Week 5 defeat at the hands of the Lions. His 44.9 passer rating on deep balls is the worst among regular starters not named Justin Herbert.

The Primary Threat: Carson Beck, who was a third-round pick in April after tearing up the ACC at Miami in 2025, but still has to leapfrog veteran Gardner Minshew on the depth chart.

The Bench Date: Week 12 against the Commanders, which is a not-too-scary home game. Prior to that, the Cards face the Rams, Broncos, Cowboys, Seahawks, Rams again, and Chiefs. That's brutal. However, I wouldn't be surprised to see Minshew get a shot in the midst of that tough stretch.

The Problem: While the Browns are competitive and Watson has bought himself some extra rope with a decent start to the season, he's averaged fewer than 5.0 yards per attempt in two of his last three starts. The Browns have the league's fifth-lowest-scoring offense and might eventually seek a spark elsewhere.

The Primary Threat: Shedeur Sanders, who made the Pro Bowl despite struggling statistically as a rookie but has undeniable talent and is one of the most popular non-starting quarterbacks in the NFL.

The Bench Date: Week 14 against the Falcons, simply because Cleveland will likely have slid out of contention by then. If Watson hasn't bounced back by December, a relatively safe home date with Atlanta provides an ideal spot to evaluate Sanders before the front office faces major offseason decisions.

The Problem: Jones is the league's third-lowest-rated qualified passer. He's thrown just three touchdown passes in five games and is just 9-for-28 with a 50.9 rating on deep attempts. Meanwhile, the Colts are 2-3 and falling well behind the first-place Jaguars in the AFC South.

The Primary Threat: Anthony Richardson, who was a top-five draft pick three years ago and is still only 24 years old. He remains a uniquely talented quarterback, and Indianapolis needs to determine whether he still has a future there.

The Bench Date: Week 17 at the Browns, with the Colts likely eliminated from playoff contention and facing a potentially favorable matchup. Indianapolis paid Jones in the offseason and will likely give him every opportunity to make this work before potentially giving Richardson another audition. That assumes neither quarterback is traded in the coming weeks.

The Problem: No matter how well Cousins plays, he'll always be a bridge to rookie No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza. And while the 38-year-old has generally performed well for a 3-2 team, he's been far from a model of consistency, and the Raiders have lost back-to-back games.

The Primary Threat: Mendoza, who made his NFL debut in relief of Cousins late in a blowout loss to the Patriots in Week 5. For now, head coach Klint Kubiak insists Cousins remains the starter.

The Bench Date: Week 12 at the Browns, giving Cousins plenty of rope while allowing Mendoza sufficient time to marinate. The Raiders, who have a dreadful schedule between now and the end of November, will likely have fallen out of the playoff picture by the time they play Cleveland in that spot.

The Problem: The experiment is not working, as Willis ranks last among qualified quarterbacks in passer rating and the Dolphins are 0-5 with the NFL's second-lowest-scoring offense.

The Primary Threat: Kyle McCord, a second-year quarterback who shined at Syracuse in 2024 before being drafted in the sixth round in 2025. Not exactly a marquee challenger, especially considering this regime paid Willis handsomely to move over from Green Bay alongside general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and head coach Jeff Hafley.

Hafley said recently that Willis' job is not in peril, citing a lack of overall support as a significant factor in his struggles. And he's probably not wrong.

The Bench Date: Week 18 at the Patriots, merely giving the staff a chance to see McCord in an otherwise meaningless affair.

The Problem: The full Jameis Experience is not for the faint of heart. While Winston technically has zero losses on his record since taking over for the injured Jaxson Dart, his lows usually more than cancel out his highs. We also know what the 32-year-old's ceiling looks like.

The Primary Threat: J.J. McCarthy, who was a top-10 pick in Minnesota two years ago and was acquired by the Giants after Dart went down. The 23-year-old struggled with the Vikings but saw some change-of-pace action in Week 5. It's certainly possible he'll find his groove if given an opportunity in a fresh setting like this one.

The Bench Date: When Dart returns in 2027 at the earliest. The Giants appear capable of hanging around all season in the fun house that is the NFC East, and Winston gives them a much better shot than McCarthy. McCarthy still needs significant development, and a potential playoff race isn't the ideal setting for it.

The Problem: The 0-5 Titans have the league's lowest-scoring offense. Ward has thrown for at least 200 yards just once this season and has completed just seven deep passes in five games.

The Primary Threat: Mitchell Trubisky, who hasn't started an NFL game since 2023 and would likely just take over if the team were to decide that Ward would be best served taking some time off. For what it's worth, they're standing firmly by Ward right now.

The Bench Date: 2027, if the Titans draft or acquire a quarterback they view as an upgrade with comparable or greater upside. Until then, there's little reason to pull the plug.

articles.title: 5 Big Questions Surrounding the Cleveland Browns Entering Week 6
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns enter Week 6 as a 3-2 enigma ahead of a home game against the Baltimore Ravens.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns enter Week 6 as a 3-2 enigma ahead of a home game against the Baltimore Ravens.

On one hand, 3-2 is a better mark than most would have expected going into the season. On the other hand, they still have a negative point differential and sit at 27th in ESPN's FPI metric .

So while the standings say the Browns are second in the AFC North, there are still a lot of questions out there that will form the narrative of the 2026 season.

Let's take a look at five of the biggest questions that need to be answered over the next several weeks.

Will Deshaun Watson Be the Starter the Whole Season?

Watson was named the starter at the beginning of the season because Todd Monken and his staff believed he gave them the best chance to win . The Browns do have a winning mark, so there may have been some validity to that, but it hasn't always been pretty.

Watson ranks 21st in Total QBR , so he's just slightly below average (which is 50). The Browns are also the most penalized team in the league, so the offensive operation hasn't been super clean.

Watson is in the final year of his contract so this is his last chance to prove he can be the Browns quarterback—or an NFL starter for that matter.

Thus far, he's played just well enough to avoid overt heat. That could change if he puts together a few disappointing games.

The Browns also have Shedeur Sanders on the bench. The second-year pro just hired an agent after being self-represented up to this point.

My prediction is that Watson won't start the whole season. He might not play himself out of the job, but his extensive injury history and the 3.8 sacks he's taking per game raise concerns about his ability to stay healthy.

Right now, the Browns' best "run" play is when Deshaun Watson runs around and scrambles. Outside of that, Cleveland has barely been able to move the ball on the ground.

They rank 29th in rushing EPA per play . Quinshon Judkins is averaging three yards per carry— 0.48 yards fewer than expected per attempt .

The difficulties on the ground are multi-faceted. The offensive line has not opened up a ton of run lanes. Judkins has run right into his blockers in some instances when they have blocked well.

LeCharles Bentley brought up a great point about how the Browns' reliance on running out of the shotgun has hindered their scheme. That stems from Deshaun Watson's preference for being in the gun, though.

Judkins, the line and the scheme itself all share in the blame. That's actually good news, because it means some things are fixable. Rebuilding the offensive line midseason would mean the run game is doomed.

Monken makes enough adjustments within the scheme and the new offensive line jells enough to show improvement. Don't expect miracles, but there's a chance the run game is closer to the middle of the pack by the end of the year.

Can the Offensive Line Turn Things Around?

It's hard to quantify offensive line play, but most metrics that attempt to do so don't look good for Cleveland. False starts and holding penalties have been recurring problems. The Browns also rank 29th in yards before contact in the run game and 27th in pressure rate allowed.

The answer to the first two questions probably lies in the answer to the third. The Browns' offense has a hard time establishing consistency and much of that can be traced to a questionable offensive line.

The reality is that the unit is playing down to its talent. The current starting five is completely different from last season. Spencer Fano and Austin Barber are both rookies. Zion Johnson, Elgton Jenkins and Tytus Howard are all newcomers who haven't played with one another.

The unit should continue to jell this season. Improved communication and familiarity as a unit give a real path to improvement.

There are some things that can be improved. Better communication and experience as a unit will take care of some operational and communication inefficiencies.

But Tytus Howard's pass protection might be an issue that can't be fixed. Fano and Barber are going to have some moments when they look like rookies.

Getting to slightly below average by the end of the year might be the ceiling.

5 Big Questions Surrounding the Buffalo Bills 🤨

Predicting When Vulnerable Starting Quarterbacks Get Benched ☹️

Can the Defense Continue to Keep Them in Games?

Because the defense has kept them in every game since Week 1's blowout loss to the Jaguars. Mike Rutenberg was an unknown going into the season as the defensive coordinator, but he has them playing well right now.

The only question is whether the unit can really keep showing up like this despite injuries and the attrition of the season.

The primary barrier to the Browns continuing to have success is injuries. The team already has key players in Mason Graham, Maliek Collins, Mike Hall Jr., Grant Delpit and Carson Schwesinger on the injury list.

Some of the players are going to play, but the length of the list is not encouraging given that we are only five weeks into the season. The team doesn't get a bye week until Week 11 this season.

There are also legitimate holes in the current defense, including a defensive line that can give up too much in the run game and inconsistent coverage from the slot and one safety position.

The grind of a late bye week and some better offenses will shift the narrative as the season goes on. The Browns are 15th in defensive EPA , which puts them closer to average than the narrative they've created over the first few weeks.

A potential matchup against Lamar Jackson on Sunday would give us a much better idea of how good the unit really is. For now, they look like a group that will wear down as the season goes.

Buyers or Sellers at the Trade Deadline?

The Browns have been to the playoffs just three times since 1999. Sneaking into the postseason might not be a big deal for other teams, but it's notable in Cleveland.

If the team finds itself in the playoff hunt ahead of the November 10 trade deadline, it would make some sense to get aggressive. At the same time, there's at least one veteran who could be on the move.

The team is already involved in the rumor mill. Jerry Jeudy has been a topic of discussion with reports that the team is looking for a third- or fourth-round pick for the veteran. There's also reporting that the Browns aren't looking to shop him at all.

Jeudy has a tradeable contract and could have a market as a former Pro Bowler.

However, the Browns could also find a veteran on the trade block that could help them break into the playoff race. That would be an opportunity that would be hard to ignore.

They'll be a seller. The Browns' record might have them in the running for a playoff spot, but it won't be enough to convince them to part with draft capital in a trade.

Andrew Berry appears to be on a hot streak with his last two drafts. Getting capital back for Jeudy would give them more opportunities for Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion while also creating more bites at the apple for the general manager.

articles.title: 5 Big Questions Surrounding the Buffalo Bills Entering Week 6
articles.summary: Five weeks, five questions.
articles.body:
As the Buffalo Bills prepare for a pre-bye matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders, they find themselves with plenty of potential issues for a first-place team with just one loss on their record.

Here are a handful that stand out as Buffalo moves into the heart of the season.

Don't get me wrong: Cook is a star. The reigning rushing yardage leader is on track for a fourth consecutive Pro Bowl season.

That said, it feels like it's only a matter of time before the 27-year-old's ball security issues cost the Bills a game.

Cook has now fumbled four times this season, and that's not an anomaly for a player who also had six fumbles in 2025 and four in 2023. That makes 10 since the start of last season, which is twice as many as any running back in the NFL except Bijan Robinson (six) in that time frame. And nine of those fumbles have come just in his last 14 regular-season games, while he added another one in last year's playoffs.

This has become a legitimate concern, and the head coach doesn't deny that.

"I don't want to lose sight of how great he is running the ball right now. But putting the ball on the ground, it's negating all the positive," Joe Brady said this week . "It's going to cost us football games. It almost cost us one."

The offense went back to Cook after he coughed the ball up in overtime Monday against the Rams, but I'd have to imagine the margin for error has shrunk dramatically.

Backups Ty Johnson and Ray Davis rarely get carries but have been factors in the passing game and certainly have the talent to take more reps from Cook. Davis has zero fumbles on 204 career touches, while Johnson's career fumble-to-touch rate is 1.1 percent (compared to 1.5 percent for Cook).

Eventually, Brady might have to consider being proactive rather than reactive if Cook continues to put the ball on the ground.

Dalton Kincaid was one of the top offensive weapons in the league during the first two weeks of the season, amassing 225 yards on 12 receptions in victories over the Texans and Lions.

He caught five 20-plus-yard passes in those two outings, but since then he has just a single 20-yard reception and has been held to just four catches for 52 total yards.

In each of his last two games, Kincaid has just a single seven-yard grab (although he did score a two-point conversion against the Rams).

What's going on? There's no indication Kincaid is hurt, but DJ Moore's shoulder injury could be affecting his production. Moore's absence may have allowed opposing defenses to devote more attention to Kincaid, arguably Buffalo's next-best pass-catching weapon.

That could explain why the 26-year-old former first-round pick has been targeted just seven times over the last three weeks. It's not as though he's losing out on contested balls or dropping passes—he's simply not a factor at all. Part of that is good defense, especially from the Patriots, who were extremely physical with Kincaid and may have thrown him off as a result.

That said, Brady absolutely has to do a better job of scheming Kincaid open, because it's hard to see the Bills contending this year without more consistent production from their top receiving tight end.

Speaking of inconsistent performances this season, Bills left tackle Dion Dawkins has looked like a future Hall of Famer in several outings and has also looked like a washed-up liability in several others.

Dawkins was a mess against New England before dominating the Rams. I've given first-year starter Alec Anderson a grade of B or higher just once in five games, and it's been a mixed bag for the rest of the starters (with the caveat that I think O'Cyrus Torrence is having a career year).

Here's the thing: Dawkins is 32, Connor McGovern is about to turn 29, and the now-injured Spencer Brown is also 28. None are super old, but none are super young. They also have a combined 299 career starts.

As a contender in win-now mode, you want experience and continuity along the line. Buffalo has plenty of that, even with Anderson replacing departed veteran David Edwards at left guard. But I'm also starting to wonder if this unit actually peaked in what was a dominant 2024 campaign, especially from a pass-blocking standpoint.

The group remains elite when it comes to carving out gaps for Cook and turning Allen loose in the running game, but it has shown signs of fading in terms of its ability to protect the franchise quarterback and avoid killer mistakes.

It's worth monitoring if you're Brady and Pete Carmichael, even if there's only so much that can be done at this juncture.

Does Josh Allen Actually Have to Do Everything?

This really ties into the previous three questions. As mentioned, Cook's ball security is a concern, Kincaid has been underutilized, Moore has struggled with injuries, and the offensive line isn't as strong as it used to be.

Could that explain why it feels as though Allen is putting it all on his shoulders to a greater extent than usual?

I mean, Allen playing Superman isn't new. But you just get the sense he's playing with more fire than ever this year. Maybe it's the fact he's 30 now, which, combined with all of the above, leaves you holding your breath every time he takes off on a YOLO scramble that concludes with anything but a safe, no-contact slide.

Three of Allen's four interceptions have come on what most would consider to be "hero balls," and he's been lucky to avoid picks on several other questionable decisions in which he's tried to force plays that carried significantly more risk than reward.

Nobody expects Allen to change his style now, but the offense may need to take some pressure off No. 17. That likely means relying more on Cook outside of obvious run-to-set-up-the-pass scenarios, or even Johnson or Davis if Cook can't hold onto the football. And it may mean rethinking the system to actually target the team's three skilled tight ends more frequently as early reads that don't leave Allen scrambling as often.

Or the team could simply keep betting on Allen's heroics, hoping the good outweighs the bad and the nine-year veteran avoids a major injury despite another season of constant punishment.

What Should They Do About the Defensive Back Seven?

The good news is Buffalo's defensive front is mega. That unit is deep across the board, with standouts Greg Rousseau, Bradley Chubb and Deone Walker well supported by the likes of Ed Oliver, T.J. Sanders, Greg Gaines and DeWayne Carter.

The bad news is the rest of the defense has been toothless through five weeks.

Off-ball linebackers Terrel Bernard and Dorian Williams have struggled to make impact plays and maintain their positioning, while the secondary's usage raises questions about new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's confidence in the unit.

Starting cornerbacks Christian Benford and Maxwell Hairston have struggled mightily and are now giving opposing receivers so much cushion that it's become laughable. Veteran offseason acquisition Dee Alford has not made a positive impact as the nickel, rookie Davison Igbinosun is a work in progress, and strong safety Cole Bishop has seemingly regressed in his second season as a regular starter.

The result? A 28th-ranked scoring defense surrendering 28.2 points per game and an AFC-worst 280.4 passing yards per outing.

This isn't working, and it should have Buffalo considering all of its options between now and the Nov. 10 trade deadline. I'm surprised they haven't brought in Tre'Davious White, who started 16 games for the Bills last season and remains an unrestricted free agent.

Meanwhile, at linebacker, Matt Milano and Shaq Thompson played a combined 1,165 defensive snaps for Buffalo last season, and both remain viable options—Milano as a free-agent signing and Thompson as a practice-squad elevation.

Beyond that, I'd be calling the Commanders about former Bill Rasul Douglas, and the Cardinals about walk-year veteran Mack Wilson, for starters.

It's possible this unit improves naturally as the personnel becomes more accustomed to Leonhard's system. But the season isn't young anymore, so general manager Brandon Beane had better have a backup plan.

articles.title: Predicting the NFL's Most Aggressive Trade Deadline Buyers in 2026 Amid More Cowboys Rumors
articles.summary: The 2026 NFL trade deadline is less than a month away, and we're sure to see some of the league's playoff hopefuls take an aggressive approach.
articles.body:
The 2026 NFL trade deadline is less than a month away, and we're sure to see some of the league's playoff hopefuls take an aggressive approach.

While the NFL's trade deadline still isn't as active as those in other major sports, it is trending in that direction. Last year, we saw the likes of Jaelan Phillips, Quinnen Williams, Sauce Gardner, Jakobi Meyers, and Rashid Shaheed change teams ahead of the deadline.

Already this season, we've seen deals involving high-profile players like Cam Jurgens, Joey Porter Jr., and Marvin Harrison Jr. More are bound to follow. In fact, the Dallas Cowboys, who added Porter, might not be done swinging deals.

According to NFL Insider Jason La Canfora , others around the league believe that Cowboys owner Jerry Jones is still poking around the trade market.

Would the 2-3 Cowboys actually be big buyers at the deadline for the second straight season? Which other teams are likely to aggressively pursue talent? Let's examine the NFL landscape, the contenders' biggest weaknesses, the recent front office histories, and the latest trade buzz to make some predictions.

The Buffalo Bills have looked like one of the top contenders in the AFC through five weeks, though they certainly don't have a flawless roster.

Their defense ranks 30th in yards allowed, and injuries to players like Ed Oliver and Dee Alford haven't helped matters.

Offensively, the Bills lack depth at wide receiver, in part because D.J. Moore has been in and out of the lineup with a shoulder injury.

Moore was, of course, one of Buffalo's marquee offseason additions. He was acquired from the Chicago Bears, along with a fifth-round pick, in exchange for a second-rounder. It wouldn't be a surprise to see GM Brandon Beane take another big swing at the trade market now.

The Bills have just $4.7 million in cap space and would need to either tweak existing contracts or target budget-friendly players to make moves. However, adding to their receiving corps or secondary would make a ton of sense.

One reason why wideout Jerry Jeudy landed on Bleacher Report's trade block big board is his modest $1.5 million base salary. B/R's Alex Kay recently named cornerback Kelee Ringo as a sensible target for Buffalo because of his rookie contract. Despite limited cap space, the Bills can make moves if they so choose.

The Chicago Bears are sitting at 3-2 and chasing the undefeated Minnesota Vikings in the NFC North. While Caleb Williams' hamstring injury played a role in both losses, a suspect defense hasn't helped.

The Bears' defense has looked respectable at times, but it ranks 22nd in yards per carry allowed and 30th in net yards per pass attempt allowed. Don't be surprised if general manager Ryan Poles looks to bolster the defensive front and the pass rush in the coming weeks.

Chicago's defense has produced 12 sacks, but it also just lost Montez Sweat to a two-game suspension for a violation of the league's PED policy. The Bears have already been linked to Los Angeles Chargers pass-rusher Khalil Mack, who tops B/R's latest trade board .

"Mack to Chicago is something multiple league sources told me makes the most sense if both teams continue on their respective trajectories," The Athletic's Jonathan Jones wrote.

Adding Mack, who has three sacks and 10 quarterback pressures, would make plenty of sense for Chicago, which has $11.4 million in cap space available. Pass-rushers like Josh Sweat and Josh Uche would also make for sensible targets.

The Cowboys made a splashy move for Williams at last year's deadline, and they've already traded for Porter and Rashan Gary since the start of the offseason. Unfortunately, Dallas' flurry of additions hasn't yielded a playoff-caliber defense.

The Cowboys entered Week 6 ranked 31st in yards allowed and 25th in points allowed. They need more defensive help, and many folks around the league believe they could trade to add it.

"Oh, Jerry is definitely doing something else," one unnamed GM said, per La Canfora , writing for Casino.guru.

"I checked in on this, and a source told me they're going to turn over every stone in an attempt to get this thing fixed," Jones wrote .

Dallas has already dealt one of its 2027 first-round picks and its third-rounder, along with its 2028 second-round pick. However, the Cowboys do have $15.5 million in cap space and feel likely to pursue more defensive talent before November 10.

A marquee pass-rusher like Mack would make sense, as would another corner, a linebacker, or perhaps a versatile safety like Budda Baker.

Like the Cowboys, the Detroit Lions have an offense that is good enough to keep them in most games and a defense that can cost them wins against virtually any opponent.

The Lions are 3-2 but rank 32nd in yards allowed and 29th in points allowed. It's hard to envision them staying in the NFC North mix without adding to a defense that is both lacking in depth and hampered by injuries.

General manager Brad Holmes hasn't been ultra-aggressive when adding talent in-season, but he did trade for pass-rusher Za'Darius Smith at the 2024 deadline. He was also pursuing Porter before he landed with Dallas, according to Lions head coach Dan Campbell.

"We were very much in on him," Campbell told reporters of Porter (h/t Bleacher Report's Mike Chiari ).

Expect the Lions to focus heavily on adding secondary help over the next few weeks. A safety like Baker could make sense, but after missing out on Porter, Holmes might prioritize cornerbacks like Ringo, Donte Jackson or Riq Woolen.

Detroit has $35.1 million in cap space with which to work.

No list of potential deadline buyers would be complete without the Los Angeles Rams. This is because L.A. general manager Les Snead has an extensive history of making aggressive moves.

We saw it in the past when Los Angeles went after players like Matthew Stafford and Von Miller. We saw it over the offseason, as Snead made trades for cornerback Trent McDuffie and pass-rusher Myles Garrett.

Of course, Snead might have to look at more budget-friendly targets at the deadline. L.A. has $8.4 million in cap space and a shrinking pool of tradable draft assets.

Thanks to those recent deals, the Rams are down to four 2027 draft picks, and they are without their 2028 second-rounder.

A low-salary wideout such as Jeudy could help fill out the Rams' receiver corps, while a rotational linebacker like Cedric Gray or Ivan Pace might be among the most realistic targets. However, it will surprise no one if Snead somehow swings another deal for a legitimate star between now and November 10.

There are a few reasons why the Pittsburgh Steelers could be aggressive at the trade deadline. They are looking to start the Mike McCarthy era off with a bang while also finding some playoff success in Aaron Rodgers' final season at quarterback.

The Steelers haven't won a playoff game since the 2016 season.

Pittsburgh is also running low on capable receivers. Michael Pittman Jr. is on injured reserve, Roman Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks , and Ben Skowronek is out with a calf injury.

General manager Omar Khan, meanwhile, has extra draft capital with which to work following the trades of Porter and Broderick Jones. According to Mark Kaboly of The Pat McAfee Show , Pittsburgh is expected to be a deadline buyer:

The Steelers probably won't pry Jeudy away from the rival Cleveland Browns, but they might be able to make a run at another potential receiving target like Brian Thomas Jr., Jauan Jennings, or Quentin Johnston. And while receiver depth is Pittsburgh's biggest need, it could also look to bolster a pass defense that ranks 22nd in net yards per attempt allowed.

Pittsburgh has $15.5 million in cap space available.

It would actually be a significant surprise if the San Francisco 49ers don't make a move or two ahead of this year's trade deadline.

They have looked like the best team in football through the first five weeks, but they have also suffered several significant injuries already.

The 49ers defense has been without star pass-rusher Nick Bosa because of a calf injury. Their offense is now missing fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and wide receiver Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and could be for the foreseeable future.

On top of multiple key injuries, San Francisco has a roster filled with aging stars like Christian McCaffrey, George Kittle, Trent Williams, and Mike Evans. This could be the team's last legitimate chance to chase a Super Bowl as currently constructed.

Oh, and John Lynch has more available cap space ($47.2 million) at his disposal than any other GM in the league.

Lynch added edge-defender Keion White at last year's deadline and should be even more aggressive this year. The 49ers could use another premier pass-rusher like Mack, a defensive lineman like Solomon Thomas, or a cornerback like Woolen. Adding to the receiver room would also be very logical.

Coincidentally, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network recently told The Pat McAfee Show that Jennings is a name to watch on the trade market. He hasn't made a substantial impact in the Minnesota Vikings' offense this season, but Jennings had 1,618 yards and 15 touchdowns over the last two seasons in San Francisco.

articles.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick Rips Bo Nix for 'Almost Disrespectful' QB Play, 'Doesn't Want to Throw The Ball'
articles.summary: The Denver Broncos improved to 4-2 thanks to an overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night, but Bo Nix's play through six games this season has led to a lot of frustration from fans and analysts.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos improved to 4-2 thanks to an overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks on Thursday night, but Bo Nix's play through six games this season has led to a lot of frustration from fans and analysts.

Following the Broncos' 17-14 victory over Seattle, Ryan Fitzpatrick said on the Prime Video postgame show that Nix's play is "almost disrespectful" for the quarterback position.

Asked to specify what he means, Fitzpatrick said Nix "doesn't want to throw the football" because he is only targeting the flats and receivers behind the sticks.

Nix has thrown for fewer than 200 yards four times in six games. He has a total of 230 yards on 54 pass attempts in the last past two games.

For perspective, Nix's 4.3 yards per attempt during that period would be tied for 19th among all players in yards per carry on rushing attempts this season.

The only quarterback this season with a lower yards per attempt average than Nix's 5.6 is Atlanta Falcons undrafted rookie Jack Strand, who is at 3.9 on just 15 attempts.

If you want to give Nix some benefit of the doubt, the Broncos' opponents thus far have included the Seahawks, Kansas City Chiefs, Jacksonville Jaguars, Los Angeles Rams and San Francisco 49ers.

Those are five of the top 11 defenses in the NFL by EPA per play. Next week should offer some respite for Nix when the Broncos play the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: NFL faces backlash over $7 million charity pledge linked to $60 million QB's suspension
articles.summary: Four years after the NFL announced a $7 million commitment to charities following Deshaun Watson’s suspension, questions are emerging about where the
articles.body: Four years after the NFL announced a $7 million commitment to charities following Deshaun Watson’s suspension, questions are emerging about where the money went. A report by FOIAball journalist David Covucci alleges that some of the funds were used for the league’s own training programmes instead of going entirely to outside nonprofits. The findings have renewed scrutiny of the NFL’s promise to support survivors and prevent sexual misconduct. While the available information does not establish that the entire amount went undelivered, it raises concerns about transparency and whether the league fulfilled its original commitment.NFL’s $7 million charity pledge faces scrutiny over fund distributionThe commitment followed Watson’s 11-game suspension in August 2022. The NFL also fined the Cleveland Browns quarterback $5 million, while the league and the Browns each pledged an additional $1 million for charitable causes, bringing the announced total to $7 million.The NFL described its intended use in its original statement.“This fund will support the work of non-profit organizations across the country that educate young people on healthy relationships, promote education and prevention of sexual misconduct and assault, support survivors, and related causes,” the league said.However, Covucci’s investigation raised questions about how much money reached outside organisations. According to his report, the NFL Foundation distributed approximately $2.3 million over three years to charities focused on sexual abuse and misconduct prevention.The league reportedly directed Covucci to four organisations that had received a combined $600,000. It also acknowledged that some of the pledged money was being used for “harassment education and training programs across the league.”That explanation has become a central point of concern. The original announcement focused on supporting nonprofit organisations, survivors and prevention efforts. Using part of the funds for internal league training raises questions about whether that spending matched the commitment presented to the public.The Browns’ separate $1 million pledge also remains unclear. Team owners Dee and Jimmy Haslam had previously expressed a commitment to prevention programmes in Northeast Ohio, but the report did not establish whether the team fulfilled that specific financial promise.Deshaun Watson’s suspension and legal controversy explainedWatson faced 24 civil lawsuits from massage therapists who accused him of sexual assault and inappropriate conduct during appointments. He denied wrongdoing and maintained that any sexual contact was consensual. In March 2022, grand juries in two Texas counties declined to indict him following criminal complaints from 10 women.The NFL conducted its own investigation. Former federal judge Sue L. Robinson initially imposed a six-game suspension after finding that the league had proved sexual assault, as defined by its policy, against four therapists. Following an appeal, the NFL and the NFL Players Association agreed to an 11-game suspension and a $5 million fine.Watson also had to undergo mandatory evaluation and treatment. His suspension cost him approximately $690,000 in salary, bringing his direct financial penalties to $5.69 million.The latest charity funding questions shift attention from Watson’s punishment to the league’s accountability. The report does not establish that the full $7 million was withheld from charities, nor does it provide a complete breakdown of the funds used for internal training.For now, the key question remains how much reached independent nonprofits and whether the NFL and Browns delivered on their original commitments. articles.title: Sam Darnold Laments His 'BS' Turnovers After Throwing 2 INTs in Seahawks' Loss to Broncos
articles.summary: Sam Darnold is shouldering the blame after his two interceptions cost the Seattle Seahawks in a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Sam Darnold is shouldering the blame after his two interceptions cost the Seattle Seahawks in a 17-14 overtime loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Darnold lamented his "B.S." turnovers for wasting another terrific effort by the Seattle defense.

"I just think it's B.S for me to keep turning the ball over," Darnold said. "It's not fair to our defense, it's not fair to out special teams group, not fair really to the entire team. So I've got to be better that way."

Not counting Week 1 when he was on the field for just five snaps against the New England Patriots due to an injury, Darnold has at least one turnover in every game he has played this season.

In three of the four games, Darnold has thrown two interceptions. His two picks on Thursday night came late in the fourth quarter and on the first possession of overtime.

Darnold got bailed out on his first interception with 1:30 remaining because the Seahawks defense forced a quick three-and-out that got the ball back. He did get them into Broncos territory to set up the game-tying field goal.

On the first possession of overtime, though, Darnold tried to force a pass to Rashid Shaheed into double coverage that Ja'Quan McMillian picked off to set up Denver's game-winning field goal three plays later.

Even though Darnold took responsibility for his turnovers, Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald was critical of the protection up front.

"Our quarterback got hit too much today," Macdonald said . "We've got to do a better job protecting him and we've got to be more decisive with the football. We don't want to take those hits, but they rushed and covered well."

Darnold was sacked five times and hit 17 times. He has been sacked a total of 13 times in the last three games.

Even though Darnold is going to be at the center of criticism for his play — and he has been bad — the issues with Seattle's offense extend beyond the quarterback.

The Seahawks can't run the ball right now. They have the third-worst EPA per play on rushing attempts in the NFL, ahead of only the Las Vegas Raiders and Green Bay Packers.

They weren't necessarily an efficient rushing attack last season, but the combination of Zach Charbonnet and Kenneth Walker III at least made them respectable on the ground.

Another issue facing the Seahawks is opposing teams don't have to worry about any wide receiver beyond Jaxon Smith-Njigba. He has 49 receptions for 717 receiving yards through six games. Shaheed, Cooper Kupp and Tory Horton combined have 35 receptions for 408 yards.

Darnold isn't helping the situation with an NFL-high seven interceptions, but he has always been a high variance player whose success depends on the talent around him.

Right now, the Seahawks don't have a strong infrastructure to protect Darnold from his worst instincts. The result is the defending Super Bowl champions are 3-3 through six games, matching their loss total from all of 2025.

Things won't get easier for Darnold and the Seahawks next week when they host the Kansas City Chiefs on Sunday Night Football.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes: Is Kansas City Chiefs quarterback entering Tom Brady-like second half of Hall of Fame career?
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes is returning from a torn ACL at the end of last season and looks back to his best; will Kansas City Chiefs put together second half of career reminiscent of Tom Brady; watch Chiefs vs Chargers live on Sky Sports on Sunday at 9.25pm
articles.body:
NFL fans and media tend to adopt a short-term view.

The hottest new star takes the headlines over the productive veteran. Those who win too much become villains, and those who beat them are heroes. Before you know it, the new heroes are winning too much for our liking.

Mahomes has been through this story arc: the incredible, exciting first season as the AFC quarterback who could finally knock Tom Brady off his throne. The Super Bowl win that rejuvenated a franchise. Then came the flag-drawing, fan-ire-inciting run to an almost 'three-peat' that turned most of the NFL world against the Mahomes/Travis Kelce/Taylor Swift media storm.

Mahomes was too good for too long. "You either die a hero, or you live long enough to see yourself become the villain," or something along those lines.

Then last season happened. Career low in quarterback rating. Career high in sack rate. A losing season (heaven forbid) along with a season-ending ACL tear. Josh Allen is Superman, Brock Purdy has reached a new level, Trevor Lawrence is breaking out. Is Mahomes... under the radar?

Let's remind ourselves of Mahomes' first eight seasons as an NFL starter.

It is unprecedented. Not since the second half of Tom Brady's remarkable career has a quarterback and team achieved this consistent level of success.

As mentioned above, we are always drawn to the hottest new star in the league, and Mahomes' first season was arguably the greatest campaign by a quarterback in their first as a starter.

After sitting behind veteran Alex Smith in his rookie year, Mahomes exploded with 5,097 passing yards and 50 touchdowns in 2018. Only Peyton Manning had reached those marks in a single season before, and Mahomes was named MVP.

It didn't take long for him to get his first Lombardi Trophy as part of a stretch that saw the Chiefs reach seven consecutive AFC Championship games, make five Super Bowls and win three.

But from new, exciting and lovable, the narrative (and style of play) changed along the way.

After that 50-TD campaign, there was a stretch where Mahomes looked unstoppable, culminating in another 5,000-yard year in 2022, with an MVP award and Super Bowl win to boot.

From 2023 onwards, his passing numbers dropped. He stopped going deep (at least compared to before). The defense also got better and although it didn't stop the team's success, we'd become used to 'video game numbers'.

It was widely celebrated when the Chiefs fell off last season, as if other teams finally knew their chance had come. That might not last long.

Will post-ACL Mahomes match Brady's 'second career'?

There is a notion that you can take the first half of Tom Brady's career and that would be enough to put him in the Hall of Fame. You could take the second half alone and say the same. Put them together and there's no denying he is the best to do it.

Somewhere in that first half, Brady tore his ACL and missed an entire campaign. The Patriots lost their opening playoff games in both seasons after he returned. Would he ever return to his Super Bowl-winning ways?

Eight seasons and eight AFC Championship appearances followed, with three Vince Lombardi Trophies and two Super Bowl losses along the way.

Safe to say he didn't 'lose it' after the injury.

Brady was 31 when he suffered that season-ending knee injury. Mahomes is 31 in his comeback season this year.

From a talent perspective, there is already an argument to be made that no one tops Mahomes. Has there ever been a better start to a career? What separates Brady is his longevity: 23 years in the league, 48 games in the playoffs, seven Super Bowl wins.

Mahomes needs to play another decade and double his Super Bowl victories to even get close to Brady's career, but if the start of this season is anything to go by, he is right back to his very best.

His quarterback rating (106.2) is at its best since 2020, his TD rate (7.0) is the closest to 2018, and his yards per attempt of 8.8 fits in more with his early-career run than recent seasons. He is playing aggressive and clean.

The Chiefs are 4-0 and putting up 412 yards per game (second-highest in the league) and 29.5 points per game (fifth). There's no denying the addition of running back Kenneth Walker is a big factor in the reinvigoration of the Chiefs' attack, but it that is also allowing Mahomes to be himself.

The Bills, Ravens and Jaguars have started out hot at 4-1, yet the Chiefs are the only team to remain undefeated in the conference (albeit with the benefit of a bye). Are we kidding ourselves that anyone other than them will represent the AFC in SoFi Stadium in February?

Kansas City will aim to go 5-0 when they face their divisional rival and 0-5 Los Angeles Chargers this Sunday, live on Sky Sports, and don't be surprised if the winning doesn't stop anytime soon.

articles.title: Week 6 Waiver Wire Best Pickups and Sleepers With FAAB Analysis, Predictions
articles.summary: Many fantasy football managers will be looking for help off the waiver wire entering the bulk of the Week 6 NFL schedule. Injuries continue to impact the fantasy landscape in a big way, and several notable stars are on bye this week.
articles.body:
Many fantasy football managers will be looking for help off the waiver wire entering the bulk of the Week 6 NFL schedule. Injuries continue to impact the fantasy landscape in a big way, and several notable stars are on bye this week.

The Cincinnati Bengals, Detroit Lions, Miami Dolphins, and Minnesota Vikings have Week 6 off.

While waiver claims have been processed in most leagues, a few standout sleeper options may still be available. Here, you'll find a look at some of the top remaining targets with analysis for leagues that utilize a free agent acquisition budget (FAAB) and some Week 6 predictions.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Finding a viable starting quarterback this late in the week is tricky, but Jameis Winston is still only rostered in 15 percent of leagues. The New York Giants' starter—who has taken over for the injured Jaxson Dart—possesses a low floor but a high ceiling.

Winston can get careless with the football but is also capable of airing it out. He has topped 20 fantasy points in each of his last two games and has a reasonable matchup at home against the New Orleans Saints this week.

The Saints have surrendered an average of 17.1 fantasy points to opposing QBs this season.

Winston is worth targeting with roughly five percent of an FAAB budget because he projects as a solid streamer/backup for the rest of the season. Dart isn't coming off of IR. He's a strong fill-in for Joe Burrow or Jared Goff this week.

Week 6 Projection: 250 passing yards, 3 TDs, 1 INT, 10 rushing yards

To be clear, Arizona Cardinals running back Tyler Allgeier doesn't have a particularly friendly matchup in Week 6. The Cardinals are set to visit the rival Los Angeles Rams, who have only surrendered the 19th-most fantasy points to opposing RBs this season.

However, Allgeier's workload could allow him to deliver for fantasy managers. He's been a complement to rookie Jeremiyah Love all season, but Love is dealing with an ankle injury and could potentially sit in Los Angeles.

"We want to get this ankle right," Cardinals coach Mike LaFleur said, per Darren Urban of the team's official website.

Allgeier is worth targeting in the range of 3-5 percent of an FAAB budget because of this week's upside and his status as a top fantasy handcuff. He's still only rostered in 44 percent of leagues.

Week 6 Prediction: 66 rushing yards, 3 receptions, 17 receiving yards, 1 TD

Pittsburgh Steelers rookie receiver Germie Bernard is worth targeting fairly aggressively because he should have solid long-term value. Michael Pittman Jr. is currently sidelined by a foot injury and has landed on injured reserve. The Steelers then lost emerging receiver Roman Wilson to a finger injury in Week 5.

Wilson is expected to miss multiple weeks.

Bernard showed that he can fill a sizeable role in Week 5, logging six receptions and 80 receiving yards. He's likely to maintain that role for the foreseeable future and can justify an FAAB of up to 10 percent of the budget—maybe even more in deeper leagues.

Bernard is only rostered in 30 percent of leagues and has an average matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (19th-most points allowed) this week.

Week 6 Projection: 5 receptions, 67 yards

articles.title: Eagles’ Jalen Hurts is ‘out indefinitely’: 5 outside options to replace him, including ex-Philly QB
articles.summary: Eagles could have to start Tanner McKee for an extended stretch: 5 QBs they could add to challenge him.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA — The recovery timeline for Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts who was diagnosed with a blood clot, varies by source.

Hurts will be out for one week or for the entire season, people say.

One doctor NJ.com spoke to on Thursday said he did not believe the blood clot would be a long-term issue, but estimated that Hurts could miss four to six weeks, depending on the severity of the blood clot and other factors, including whether he is already taking blood thinners.

NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport took it even further and said that Hurts is "out indefinitely."

If Hurts is out for an extended period this season, fourth-year backup quarterback Tanner McKee will take over as the starter until he is cleared to return — assuming he returns this season.

McKee has flashed intriguing potential in his two NFL starts. But after a bad summer, the hype has cooled down. McKee lost the backup job during training camp to Andy Dalton, though McKee reclaimed the position from Dalton before Week 4. Dalton was cut by the Eagles last week.

The Eagles have been bullish on McKee's potential for years, but they changed their tune this summer by demoting him to the third-string quarterback position.

If the Eagles aren't comfortable moving forward with McKee as their only option to replace Hurts, they could explore trading for another team's backup quarterback.

They could also re-sign Dalton, but he wouldn't be an upgrade over McKee.

Here are five potential options the Eagles could pursue if they want to add competition for McKee:

After playing two seasons for the Eagles from 2021-2022, Minshew is already comfortable playing under Eagles coach Nick Sirianni and throwing to playmakers DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert.

Philadelphia's current offense is slightly different from it was four years ago, but Minshew won't be starting from scratch.

He has started 47 games during his eight-year career, posting a 17-30 record. He has been considered one of the NFL's best backups for many years, including when he won seven of his 13 starts with the Colts in 2023.

Playing with a gunslinger mentality, Minshew has recorded 68 touchdowns and 35 interceptions in the last eight years.

For a more fun option, the Eagles could check Richardson's availability. The former first-round pick requested a trade from the Colts in February, six months after he lost the starting job to Daniel Jones.

Richardson has the highest upside among the quarterbacks listed here, but he also offers a lower floor than some QBs. He has absurd physical tools (6-4, 244 pounds), elite arm talent and top-end athleticism, but his inconsistency as a passer is the reason why he never developed into a franchise quarterback.

Richardson has recorded a 50.6% completion percentage during the first four years of his career. He has played his entire career under Colts head coach Shane Steichen, the former offensive coordinator of the Eagles from 2021-2022.

Rattler lost his starting job last year to second-round pick Tyler Shough.

He played well at times, but the Saints always planned to make Shough the starter after spending that draft capital on him.

Rattler, a former fifth-round pick, has posted a 1-13 record as a starter. But he's not the sole reason the Saints struggled during the previous two seasons. New Orleans was a bad team during Rattler's first two seasons, and the Saints have a 1-4 record this year.

Rattler, who possesses good arm talent, could develop into one of the NFL's best backups. The Saints could make former first-round pick Zach Wilson the backup if they traded Rattler elsewhere.

O'Connell would provide more depth behind McKee and could be a better option than Dalton for the Eagles' second quarterback.

In 17 career starts, he has recorded 20 touchdowns to 11 interceptions and completed 62% of his passes. He has posted a 7-10 record.

O'Connell has good size (6-3, 209 pounds) and throws an accurate ball. He is currently the Raiders' No. 3 QB, which could make him expendable.

Bennett could run the system that the Eagles hoped would transform their offense, though it has not yet worked.

As the Rams' backup, he has a good understanding of the West Coast passing attack, but due to his lack of experience — zero starts across four seasons and just 13 career passing yards — he wouldn't be the Eagles' best option.

articles.title: Bo Nix, Broncos Make Strange Statistical History in OT Win vs. Sam Darnold, Seahawks
articles.summary: Even though Denver Broncos fans would like to see their team win a game with the offense looking closer to its 2025 form, the franchise did something on Thursday night it hadn't done in 43 years.
articles.body:
Even though Denver Broncos fans would like to see their team win a game with the offense looking closer to its 2025 form, the franchise did something on Thursday night it hadn't done in 43 years.

Per ESPN's Adam Schefter, the Broncos' 168 yards of total offense against the Seattle Seahawks represented their fewest in a win since John Elway's first NFL start in 1983.

Elway's first start was the season opener against the Pittsburgh Steelers. He finished 1-of-8 for 14 yards and one interception. The Broncos were outgained 314-139, but they forced seven turnovers in a 14-10 victory.

Thursday's 17-14 overtime victory over the Seahawks wasn't quite that ugly, though it's not one that will go on the offensive highlight reel for the 2026 season.

Bo Nix finished 17-of-27 for 107 yards with no touchdowns and no interceptions. The Broncos ran for 74 yards and two touchdowns on 28 carries.

The good news is Denver has won three of its last four games and sits at 4-2 going into a Week 7 matchup with the Arizona Cardinals.

articles.title: NFL Week 6 expert picks for Packers vs. Cowboys: Who wins primetime game?

articles.body:
Can the Green Bay Packers win a third straight game when the Dallas Cowboys come to Lambeau Field for a primetime showdown in Week 6? The majority of NFL experts see the Packers, who are fresh off a big win over the rival Chicago Bears , beating the Cowboys in a shootout on "Sunday Night Football."

Of the 54 experts reviewed this week, roughly 70 percent picked the Packers to win straight up. Many of those predicting a final score envisioned a game with a lot of points, which isn't surprising given the quality of the two offenses, especially at quarterback and wide receiver, and the 40-40 tie that took place between the two teams last year. Another primetime shootout between Dak Prescott and Jordan Love could be possible, maybe even likely.

A review of the Week 6 expert picks of Packers vs. Cowboys:

Of the six experts at USA Today , two picked the Packers to win.

Nick Middlehurst-Schwartz: Packers, 31-27

Of the 11 experts at ESPN , seven picked the Packers to win.

Of the five experts at NFL.com , four picked the Packers.

From Parr: "It's going to be very difficult for the Cowboys to win with their current defense, and they are running into a team that knows how to exploit their weakness on Sunday night. Dallas is the only NFL team to allow 375 or more yards in each of the first five games. The Cowboys have given up 20+ points in 12 consecutive contests dating back to last season, the league's longest active streak. At least they're consistent. Unfortunately for first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker (and new hire Mike Pettine), the Packers' offense just awoke from its slumber, with Jordan Love dropping deep throws on the Bears repeatedly last week (367 pass yards, two touchdowns). Now WRs Christian Watson and Matthew Golden -- the only teammate duo to each have 375+ receiving yards -- get to line up across from a secondary that has looked overmatched all season. I'm expecting a better showing from the Dak Prescott-led offense than the dud it produced against the Buccaneers last time out, and having a rest advantage (nine days between games versus six for the Packers) undoubtedly helps, but I have no confidence his defense will support him. Give me the home team in a shootout."

Of the eight experts at MMQB , seven picked the Packers.

Of the eight experts at The Athletic , seven picked the Packers.

Of the seven experts at CBS Sports , five picked the Packers.

From Prisco: "The Packers blew out the Bears Sunday as Jordan Love lit up the skies. Look for more of that in this one against a bad Dallas secondary. The Cowboys struggled on defense against the Bucs, and that will continue in this one. Love continues to play well. Packers win a shootout. Packers 31, Cowboys 27."

Of the nine experts at SB Nation , six picked the Packers.

articles.title: Ryan Fitzpatrick on Broncos QB Bo Nix: 'It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing football right now'
articles.summary: The "NFL on Prime" analyst unloaded on Nix after a subpar performance against the Seahawks.
articles.body:
The Denver Broncos beat the Seattle Seahawks 17-14 in overtime Thursday night, but it was not the best of displays from quarterback Bo Nix.

It was a night where Nix recorded only 107 yards on 27 pass attempts and did not throw a touchdown pass while being sacked twice. As the Broncos held a second-half lead and were looking to extend the difference, the offense ended six consecutive drives with a punt. The defense gets most of the credit for the win after recovering two fumbles and intercepting Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold twice, including in overtime .

The play of Nix was the postgame story, so much so that former longtime NFL quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick, now part of the "NFL on Prime Video" crew, could not hold back his criticisms of the third-year signal-caller.

"I'm glad they scored the two touchdowns in the first half, but they were in four-minute mode when the second half started," Fitzpatrick said. "It was really frustrating to watch. And part of it, for me, is Bo Nix is not playing competitively. It's almost disrespectful to the quarterback position how he's playing football right now."

"First of all, the guy doesn't want to throw the ball," he said. "That's fine. He's throwing to the flats, he's throwing behind, but he has no trust from his coach. He calls a screen play on third-and-8. Just run up and let the clock keep going. What does he do? He throws it away. Seattle gets the ball, they have a timeout."

Fitzpatrick's frustration with Nix then went up a level.

"And then in overtime, he's got two chances to be competitive. The last one being a designed run for him to run, make somebody miss, and get a first down for your football team! Now, they're in the locker room right now. They're excited. They won. He's not playing competitive football right now."

When host Charissa Thompson brought up how frustrated Broncos players might feel, Fitzpatrick continued saying that he feels Nix is "not competing right now" and while he wasn't sure if the quarterback is still bothered by the ankle injury suffered last season, "it's not good enough. It's effort."

What frustrated Fitzpatrick the most about what he saw in Nix's game?

"Well, there's no fire and there's no passion," Fitzpatrick said . "And that doesn't mean you've got to be yelling at guys on the sideline or inspiring in the huddle. You can do it with your play as well. And I just don't see it. And I just think that he needs to be sat down and they need to tell him being a quarterback in the NFL is a very special thing. And right now he's taking it for granted. He is. And there's a lot of guys that have played this game that watch that game that think, 'That right there is garbage. That effort is garbage. That is not a quarterback in the NFL. We deserve better.'"

The Broncos' offensive struggles have been noted and head coach Sean Payton has taken play-calling duties back from offensive coordinator Davis Webb. But it won't matter who is calling out the plays if Nix's decision-making with the ball continues to lead to inefficient offensive production.

The win improves the Broncos to 4-2. They will face the Arizona Cardinals, Kansas City Chiefs and Carolina Panthers before going on their bye week in Week 10.

articles.title: Brandon Aiyuk's Former 49ers Teammate Sounds Off on WR's 'Desperate' Antics amid Trade Push
articles.summary: Some of wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's former San Francisco 49ers teammates commented anonymously this week on the wideout's shocking fall from grace.
articles.body:
Some of wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk's former San Francisco 49ers teammates commented anonymously this week on the wideout's shocking fall from grace.

Aiyuk, 28, signed a four-year, $120 million contract with the 49ers in August 2024, but just two months later, he tore his ACL and MCL, and he has not appeared in a game since then.

The 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list late in the 2025 season after failing to update the organization on his rehab and progress.

Best and Worst Landing Spots for Potentially Available Wide Receivers 🤔

One of Aiyuk's former 49ers teammates told Michael-Shawn Dugar of The Athletic that Aiyuk was a "distraction" during the 2025 season during the time that he was around the team facility.

That teammate recalled a time when Aiyuk spoke out while 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan critiqued a player during a team meeting, noting that Aiyuk's "humility was kind of gone."

Since being placed on the reserve/left team list, Aiyuk has publicly lobbied for a trade or release so he could join the Washington Commanders and reunite with his former college teammate in quarterback Jayden Daniels.

Aiyuk even made numerous social media posts in which he was wearing Commanders gear .

Another of Aiyuk's former 49ers teammates commented on Aiyuk's actions, telling Dugar, "What I see is that he really wants to get back in. That's what the antics show to me: It shows he's desperate."

Aiyuk was once a rising NFL star, as the 2020 first-round pick out of Arizona State had back-to-back strong seasons in 2022 and 2023.

Following a campaign with 78 receptions for 1,015 yards and eight touchdowns in 2022, Aiyuk was even better the following season, recording 75 grabs for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns en route to Second Team All-Pro honors.

Now, Aiyuk is trending toward missing a second consecutive season in its entirety, as he has yet to apply for reinstatement, which he must do in order to get traded.

The Commanders signed Stefon Diggs during the offseason to pair with No. 1 wide receiver Terry McLaurin, though, which suggests Washington may not be a realistic landing spot for Aiyuk until next season at the earliest.

For now, the waiting game persists, and it is fair to wonder if or when Aiyuk will be seen again on an NFL field.
