articles.title: Joe Milton Reportedly Signed by Eagles from Cowboys' Practice Squad After Jalen Hurts' Calf Injury
articles.summary: With Jalen Hurts set to miss at least one game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot, the Philadelphia Eagles are adding more depth to their quarterback room.
articles.body:
With Jalen Hurts set to miss at least one game after being diagnosed with a superficial blood clot, the Philadelphia Eagles are adding more depth to their quarterback room.

Per NFL insider Jordan Schultz , the Eagles are signing Joe Milton to their 53-man roster after he spent the first five weeks of the season on the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad.

The Eagles' statement about Hurts' blood clot revealed it was originally discovered via ultrasound after their Saturday walkthrough leading up to their game against the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

A follow-up ultrasound on Wednesday "revealed movement in the small blood clot." Hurts has been ruled out for Week 6 against the Carolina Panthers as they "determine the appropriate course of treatment . "

Tanner McKee is set to make his third career start on Sunday. Andy Dalton, who entered this season as Philadelphia's No. 2 quarterback, was released by the club on Oct. 9.

Behind Hurts and McKee, the only other quarterback on the Eagles' roster prior to adding Milton was Cole Payton.

Payton was a fifth-round pick by Philadelphia in the 2026 draft out of North Dakota State. He went 5-of-12 for 47 yards and one touchdown in three preseason games.

Milton is in his third NFL season after being a sixth-round pick in the 2024 draft by the New England Patriots. He played one game as a rookie before being traded to Dallas in April 2025.

The Cowboys used Milton in four games last season. He went 15-of-24 for 183 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions in 2025.

Given the timing of Milton's signing, Payton would seem likely to be Philadelphia's No. 2 quarterback against the Panthers.

Depending on how long Hurts' absence ends up being, the Eagles could elevate Milton to be their primary backup at some point as he gets acclimated to the playbook.

The Eagles have lost three straight games following a 2-0 start. They are under .500 for the first time since the 2021 season.

articles.title: Week 6 NFL odds, picks, predictions: Our best bets for Sunday's games
articles.summary: Our NFL handicappers give out their favorite bets for Week 6 games.
articles.body:
Week 6 of the NFL season began with a Denver Broncos 17-14 overtime win against the Seattle Seahawks. The Broncos blew an 11-point fourth-quarter lead, but held on, thanks to two Sam Darnold interceptions.

What will the rest of the weekend have in store for bettors?

Our NFL handicapping team of Corbie Craig, Michael Fiddle, Matt Jacob, Jeremy Pond and Matt Russell combine to give their best bets for Week 6 of the NFL season.

Houston Texans vs. Jacksonville Jaguars (-2.5, 42.5) in London

Pond : Brenton Strange might be the hottest tight end in the NFL not named Trey McBride right now.

After collecting just seven receptions for 72 yards in Jacksonville's first three games, the Penn State product has caught fire, racking up 14 catches on 16 targets for 163 yards in the Jaguars' back-to-back wins against Cincinnati and Philadelphia. He also boasted a team-best 26.2% target share in those wins.

Now, Strange and Jacksonville face a Texans defense that has amassed 20 sacks, including a league-high 7 from Will Anderson Jr. The Texans are third in sack percentage and 10th in total pressures.

Lawrence is going to face the heat from Houston's nasty defensive line all day long, meaning he's going to have to get the ball out quickly to his receivers. And that's why I think Strange, who has become one of his two favorite targets — the other being Parker Washington — will prosper a third consecutive week in this showdown.

Back him to find the end zone and hit this mini ladder of receptions at plus money.

Bets: TE Brenton Strange anytime TD (+330) | 5+ receptions (+136) | 6+ receptions (+265)

New York Jets at New England Patriots (-7.5, 43.5)

Russell: Drake Maye has a particular set of skills.

Maye's quarterbacking "super power" is two-fold: An ability to scramble and a nice deep-ball. During the Patriots' two-game resurgence — wins over the Bills and Raiders — Maye ran 15 times for 79 yards, and was able to hit big shots against two of the worst pass defenses in the NFL (both in the bottom-quarter of the league in Dropback EPA/Play and Success Rate).

This week looks a little trickier, and not just because the Jets are sixth and 12th in those metrics when adjusted for garbage time and turnovers.

Will Campbell's been upgraded from doubtful, but he and right tackle Morgan Moses are both listed as questionable, on an offensive line that's given up sacks at the best of times (47 during the regular season last year, and 11 in five games this year). Until recently, that might not have been an issue against the Jets, but first-round pick David Bailey got home three times last week, and New York has 17 sacks and the seventh-best pass-rush win-rate in the league (according to ESPN).

The Jets defense struggles against the run, but with TreVeyon Henderson out, the Patriots will have to go back to the plodding-version of their run game with Rhamondre Stevenson to take the heat off Maye.

As for the Jets, Geno Smith must be staring at his weather app this week, with fingers crossed. The grim conditions for his two home games this season have tamped down his numbers, as his best games have come in beautiful summer weather at Tennessee and indoors against the Lions. While those defenses aren't impressive, Smith's bugaboo last season — interceptions — has been taken out of the equation this season completely.

On what should be crisp-but-sunny autumn conditions in Foxborough, Smith could replicate the nice day he had against the Patriots defense in Week 1 last season (24-of-34, 362 yards, TD, INT) before the Raiders' offensive line (and season) fell apart. With a pass-block win-rate as good as their defensive line numbers, Smith should have the time and conditions to keep up with Maye.

Pittsburgh Steelers (-2.5, 39.5) at Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Pond : When it comes to bare cupboards, there might not be any more empty than the one housing the Steelers' wide receivers.

Roman Wilson, Michael Pittman and Ben Skowronek are hurt. And they've all been ruled out in Pittsburgh's clash with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

So, where does QB Aaron Rodgers turn to complement DK Metcalf down in Florida? Enter Pat Freiermuth.

The standout tight end is favorite target for Rodgers when the Steelers are deep in the opposition's territory, catching four touchdowns, including two in last week's win against the Indianapolis Colts. And things got so thin at wide receiver that Freiermuth actually lined up in the relatively foreign position to him.

Now, Rodgers, Freiermuth and the Pittsburgh offense face a Tampa Bay defense allowing the sixth-most points to tight ends this season. And that should mean chances for Freiermuth in the red zone.

I like the numbers we're getting on Freiermuth to score and to clear his receptions total. Rodgers loves him and so do we at these prices.

Bets: TE Pat Freiermuth and anytime TD (+320, BetMGM) and over 3.5 receptions (+116, FanDuel)

Arizona Cardinals at Los Angeles Rams (-12.5, 51.5)

Jacob: The NFL's schedule-makers didn't do any favors for the 2026 Los Angeles Rams.

First, they sent the Rams to Australia for a divisional game against one of the league's best teams (San Francisco). Then, after a Monday night home game against the Giants, the Rams hit the road for consecutive games against Denver and Philadelphia before returning home to play Buffalo.

For context, the 49ers, Broncos, Eagles and Bills posted a combined 49-19 record last season. Add several key injuries to that early-season gauntlet, and it's hardly surprising Los Angeles is off to a 2-3 start.

Now, for the first time, the Rams are home for consecutive games. And they get a cupcake opponent that has lost 18 of its last 20 games while covering the point spread just six times. Isolate the last 10 contests, and Arizona is 1-9 SU and 2-8 ATS while allowing an average of 34.7 PPG. This includes two blowout losses to the Rams (45-17 and 37-20).

Yes, Arizona got a last-minute backdoor cover three weeks ago in a 36-30 loss at San Francisco as an 8.5-point underdog. But the 49ers were in a lookahead spot that day, with games against Denver and at Seattle on deck. This week, the Cardinals face a focused — and angry — Rams squad that is eager to show why it remains a top three Super Bowl contender.

Look for the Matthew Stafford-led offense to once again light up a wretched Cardinals defense. And look for L.A.'s stop unit to have its best performance since a 28-6 Week 2 win over the Giants.

Pond: Like my colleague, I think the Rams are going to lay the smack down on the Cardinals after that gutting Week 5 defeat against the Bills. That should translate into Arizona finding itself in another deep hole early on in this affair.

So, what does that mean for the Cardinals and quarterback Jacoby Brissett? Air out, baby. There will be no other options.

And one of the weapons Brissett will again target often is Kendrick Bourne. Bourne finished with five receptions on eight targets for 70 yards in last weekend's defeat against the Detroit Lions. That was his best statistical performance since Arizona's Week 1 victory against the winless Los Angeles Chargers when he recorded eight catches on eight targets for 75 yards.

Bourne is clear WR2 behind Michael Wilson now that Marvin Harrison Jr. is with the Houston Texans, so that will open up even more opportunities to produce on a team that seemingly is always playing from behind.

I am jumping on Bourne via two ladder plays involving receptions and receiving yards. This could be a shootout and I expect him to have a big showing against the Rams.

Bets: WR Kendrick Bourne: 4+ receptions (+116) | 5+ receptions (+240) and 40+ receiving yards (+112) | 50+ receiving yards (+182) | 60+ yards (+290) at FanDuel

Los Angeles Chargers at Kansas City Chiefs (-8.5, 42)

Fiddle: It's always hard to click the button to fade one of the hottest players in the NFL, but I think now is the right time in Kansas City.

Through four games this season — and an undefeated start — Kenneth Walker III has been the engine of the Chiefs offense. He has amassed 87 carries in those games, averaging over 21 rush attempts per game. This week, though, I think that number could drop.

The Chiefs are coming off their Week 5 bye, and head coach Andy Reid has thrived in these situational spots — he is 22-5 after the bye week. A lot of that can likely be attributed to more specific game planning and detailed play creation for the given opponent. I expect Kansas City to integrate Xavier Worthy and Cyrus Allen heavily into the game plan — and a few of those touches could come on gadget run plays, which would directly take from Walker.

The Chargers are likely to stack the box heavily and not afford Walker clean looks. They know wide receivers Rashee Rice and Tyquon Thornton are hurt, and Walker has been the focal point. I expect a heavy blitz rate and a run-stopping effort from L.A. defense, forcing the ball into Patrick Mahomes' hands to create with receivers in man coverage.

The angles I like here are a possible Mahomes over on his rushing yards, or Kenneth Walker under on his rushing attempts. From a market value perspective, the better odds are on Walker unders right now.

Bet: Kenneth Walker III under 19.5 rushing attempts (-115, BetMGM)

Dallas Cowboys at Green Bay Packers (-1.5, 53)

Jacob: Here are the final scores of the Cowboys' last 10 games away from Dallas: 37-32, 30-27, 44-24, 33-16, 44-30, 30-23, 34-17, 28-20, 34-31 and 34-30. All 10 games flew over the total.

Now here are the final scores of the Cowboys' last four regular season games against Green Bay: 35-31 (2017), 34-24 (2019), 31-28 (2022) and 40-40 (2025). And the last two playoff games against Green Bay: 34-31 (2016) and 48-32 (2023). All six flew over the total.

But wait, there's more: The over is 5-0 on Sunday Night Football this season. It also is 8-2 with totals that close at 50 points or higher. And Dallas — which is coming off an embarrassing 24-16 home loss to the Bucs that fell way short of the total — hasn't seen the under hit in consecutive games since Weeks 9 and 10 in 2024 (a stretch of 30 contests).

So of course for this SNF matchup I'm recommending the … under.

Call it an all-time contrarian play, but there's a correlated reason for it. Both quarterbacks — Dallas' Dak Prescott and Green Bay's Jordan Love — are among the NFL's best downfield passers. And they have to be, because neither gets any support from the running game (the Cowboys rank 30th in rushing; the Packers are dead last).

Here's the problem: Strong, sustained winds are forecast for Sunday night in Green Bay — the kind that hamper deep throws (as well as long field-goal attempts).

In other words, both Prescott and Love likely will have to rely on short and intermediate passes to keep drives alive. That means fewer quick-strike scores, which are usually needed for an NFL game to clear this high of a total.

No, this won't be a 14-10 defensive slugfest. Rather, I expect something in the range of 24-21 — and even that leaves a full touchdown of wiggle room.

articles.title: Ryan Clark challenges Stephen A. Smith over Lane Johnson’s retirement as Eagles star puts mental health first
articles.summary: Ryan Clark has defended Lane Johnson after Stephen A. Smith questioned the Philadelphia Eagles tackle’s decision to retire during the 2026 NFL season.
articles.body: Ryan Clark has defended Lane Johnson after Stephen A. Smith questioned the Philadelphia Eagles tackle’s decision to retire during the 2026 NFL season. Speaking on The Pivot Podcast, Clark said that a person’s intentions matter less than the effect their words have on others. He also praised Johnson for putting his mental health and family first, while pointing out why Smith’s comments deserved criticism despite his later apology.Ryan Clark tells Stephen A. Smith why Lane Johnson’s mental health mattersClark made his position clear while discussing Johnson’s retirement and the reaction to it. He said he was proud of the veteran offensive tackle for choosing what was best for him rather than forcing himself to continue playing football.“Lane Johnson’s football career has been about intent and impact. And I think more people should understand that,” Clark said on The Pivot Podcast. He also welcomed Smith’s apology but stressed that good intentions do not erase the effect a person’s words can have.“Your intent doesn’t matter. It’s about your impact. It’s about what people see in you, how you’ve changed people’s lives,” Clark added.His comments came after Smith faced criticism for the way he discussed Johnson’s decision on ESPN’s First Take. On October 7, one day after the retirement announcement, Smith questioned why Johnson had chosen to walk away when the Eagles were struggling through a difficult stretch of the season.The Eagles were 2-2 at the time and had suffered back-to-back losses. Smith also pointed to the team’s injury problems and the absence of key players, including A.J. Brown and DeVonta Smith, while questioning Johnson’s timing.During the discussion, Smith repeatedly referred to Johnson’s mental health in a sarcastic tone. That approach drew criticism because Johnson had clearly explained that his emotional well-being and family priorities were behind his decision.Clark’s response focused on the difference between questioning a player’s timing and dismissing the personal reasons behind such a major life choice. For him, Johnson’s decision showed that looking after yourself can matter more than staying in a sport, even when your team still needs you.Lane Johnson explains his retirement as Ryan Clark defends his decisionJohnson announced his retirement on October 6, bringing an end to a 14-season career with the Philadelphia Eagles. The veteran offensive lineman admitted that walking away was difficult, especially because he had hoped to play one more season alongside his teammates.“I deeply wanted to gut it out for one more year; to take the field with my brothers for one last season,” Johnson wrote in his retirement statement.However, he explained that his priorities had changed and that continuing to play was no longer the right choice for him.“Right now it is critical that I focus on my mental health. I owe it to my teammates, coaches, the organization and the fans to have my head and heart 100 percent in the game,” Johnson said. “And right now my heart is telling me that it’s time to say goodbye to football.”Johnson’s words made it clear that he did not want to continue playing unless he could give the game his full attention. articles.title: Sam Darnold's Job Security Addressed by Mike Macdonald After Seahawks' Loss to Broncos
articles.summary: Sam Darnold's status as the Seattle Seahawks' starting quarterback is secure despite struggling during the team's 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night.
articles.body:
Sam Darnold's status as the Seattle Seahawks' starting quarterback is secure despite struggling during the team's 17-14 loss to the Denver Broncos on Thursday night.

Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said that he isn't considering a change under center during a Friday appearance on Seattle Sports 710 radio.

Darnold finished 27-of-51 for 278 yards and two interceptions against the Broncos.

ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the "feeling" among "some people in the league" is that keeping Darnold as Seattle's starter is the right move.

Both of his turnovers against the Broncos were particularly costly, with the first occurring with less than 90 seconds remaining in the fourth quarter. The Seahawks, at that point, had the ball at Denver's 39-yard line while trailing by three.

Seattle was able to get the ball back and send the contest to overtime with a late field goal, but Darnold was picked off again on the first possession of the extra period.

The Seahawks weren't able to emerge victorious despite an impressive performance from their defense, limiting the Broncos to just 168 total yards as well as an average of 2.9 yards per play.

After suffering a glute injury on the opening drive of Week 1 and missing Week 2 as a result, Darnold has been inconsistent to begin the year.

He's completed 60.4 percent of his throws for 1,033 yards and seven touchdowns while throwing seven interceptions across five appearances.

The Seahawks boast one of the NFL's top backup quarterbacks in Drew Lock, who has filled in admirably for Darnold this year.

Lock threw for 422 yards and four touchdowns without getting picked off while Darnold was sidelined. His 127.3 passer rating is the No. 1 mark in the NFL, albeit in a small sample size.

The defending Super Bowl champions will be back in action next Sunday night against Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson Injury Update, Latest News on Ravens QB's Status for NFL Week 6 vs. Browns
articles.summary: Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury.
articles.body:
Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's game against the Cleveland Browns as he continues to recover from an ankle injury.

Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Jackson's status Friday, ruling him out for the matchup.

ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported that Jackson had a "realistic chance to return for Sunday's game," with Minter telling reporters that Jackson was considered day-to-day. Minter added that Jackson is "working his butt off" and "doing everything he can" to return to the field.

Jackson was out for Week 5 as Tyler Huntley led the Ravens to an overtime win at the Atlanta Falcons.

He initially left Week 4's 24-18 win over the Tennessee Titans with an ankle injury and didn't play in the second half, a concerning development for a Ravens' offense very much reliant on the dynamic quarterback's unique skill set.

While the Ravens didn't believe at the time that Jackson's injury was going to be a long-term issue, there was uncertainty over his short-term availability.

"I really don't think it's going to be crazy long term, but we'll see what happens," head coach Jesse Minter told reporters at the time.

There's no replacing a two-time MVP and three-time first-team All-Pro like Jackson, though the Ravens do have an experienced backup in Huntley.

"There's one Lamar Jackson, the guy's a two-time MVP," Minter said after Week 4. "And so I think for anybody to have to say we're being compared to Lamar is unfair and not realistic. I think [Huntley] as a backup quarterback in this league and even as a starter at times has shown the ability to come in and really kind of run the offense, make plays with his legs, be able to make plays on third down."

Injuries were also a concern for Jackson last season, as he missed four games due to a hamstring injury and a back contusion. Huntley started two of those games, leading the team to a 2-0 record. But the Ravens are obviously a much more dangerous team with a healthy Jackson.

articles.title: Jeremiyah Love Injury Update, Latest News on Status for Cardinals vs. Rams amid Ankle Issue
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals will be without Jeremiyah Love for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
articles.body:
The Arizona Cardinals will be without Jeremiyah Love for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.

Head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters on Friday that Love won't play this week because of an ankle injury he originally suffered in Week 4 against the New York Giants.

LaFleur added that the Cardinals are not currently considering putting Love on injured reserve, which would keep him out for at least four games.

Love's right ankle has disrupted his rookie season thus far. He suffered a high-ankle sprain in Arizona's preseason game against the Las Vegas Raiders on Aug. 13.

After sitting out the final two preseason games, Love was able to play in Week 1 as the No. 2 running back against the Los Angeles Chargers. He has started each of the last four games.

In Week 4 against the Giants, Love aggravated the same ankle in the second quarter. He played the entire game but was only on the field for 30 of Arizona's 66 offensive snaps in a 36-24 loss.

Love was limited for the first two days of practice last week before being upgraded to a full participant on Friday. He started against the Detroit Lions, but ran for a season-low 22 yards on 12 carries.

The Cardinals listed Love as a non-participant in their first two practices this week.

Love's absence is another wrinkle for an Arizona offense that was already going into its first game without Marvin Harrison Jr., who was traded to the Houston Texans on Monday.

Tyler Allgeier will step into the role as Arizona's starting running back. The 26-year-old has run for 119 yards and one touchdown on 35 carries in five games this season.

The Cardinals have lost four straight games since their season-opening win over the Chargers. They are seeking their first victory over the Rams since Week 2 of the 2024 season.

articles.title: Ravens, without Jackson, face familiar foe in Browns coach Monken
articles.summary: Baltimore star quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's NFL game at Cleveland with a left ankle injury but the Ravens will see a familiar face when they...
articles.body:
Baltimore star quarterback Lamar Jackson will miss Sunday's NFL game at Cleveland with a left ankle injury but the Ravens will see a familiar face when they visit the Browns.

Browns first-year head coach Todd Monken, who served as the Ravens offensive coordinator the past three seasons, guides Cleveland (3-2) against the Ravens (4-1) in a fight for the AFC North division lead.

"If I know Todd the way I think I know Todd, he will want to kick our tails," Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey said.

Monken, 60, questioned how much benefit he will have knowing the Ravens players, noting they will know his offensive schemes as well.

"I don't know about that. Gets offset by what we do on offense I guess," Monken said. "Got a lot of respect for their players. What you see is what you get from them.

"Did I enjoy my time there? Of course. A lot of really good memories. Got a lot of good friends and people there. Other than that, no, it's a divisional game."

First-year Ravens coach Jesse Minter, a former Los Angeles Chargers defensive coordinator who took over in January, will coach in his first game against a division rival.

"I've always felt like the division games mean a little bit more," Minter said. "It's just really an intent and a focus when you play division teams. It's our first crack at that."

Jackson, hurt in Baltimore's October 4 victory over Tennessee, has not practiced since and Minter said on Friday he would miss a second straught game, with Tyler "Snoop" Huntley starting for the Ravens at Cleveland after leading a comeback victory in Atlanta last Sunday.

"I've been there before where we played Snoop and Snoop is a really good football player. Won a bunch of games as a starter," Monken said.

In 2024, Monken directed the first Ravens team to throw for 4,000 yards and run for 3,000 yards in the same season.

"Todd's a great offensive play caller," Minter said. "A guy I've got a ton of respect for. They have a great defense. We're just excited for the challenge."

Two other 4-1 division leaders face tests Sunday as well, with AFC East leader Buffalo at 3-2 Las Vegas and AFC South leader Jacksonville meeting Houston (1-4) in London.

Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts was ruled out for Sunday's home game against Carolina after an ultrasound exam revealed movement in a blood clot discovered in his calf.

"Jalen will be out for Sunday's game versus the Panthers as we determine the appropriate course of treatment," the Eagles said in a statement. "His health at safety are our highest priority."

Two of the NFL's three undefeated clubs are at home this week, the Kansas City Chiefs (4-0) against the Chargers (0-5) on Sunday and the San Francisco 49ers (5-0) against Washington (1-3-1) on Monday. Minnesota (5-0) is off this week.

Sunday's other games include Chicago at Atlanta, Tennessee at Indianapolis, the New York Jets at New England, New Orleans at the New York Giants, Pittsburgh at Tampa Bay, Arizona at the Los Angeles Rams and Dallas at Green Bay.

articles.title: Stephen Ross sells 2.1 percent of Dolphins, sports properties for $12.5B
articles.summary: Chilean billionaire Jean Eric Salata will own 2.1 percent of the Dolphins as well as Hard Rock Stadium, the F1 Hard Rock Miami Grand Prix and the Miami Open...
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins owner Stephen Ross reportedly has added another minority investor to his sports portfolio.

According to Ben Fischer of Sports Business Journal, Ross has agreed to sell 2.1 percent of the team and its affiliated businesses at a valuation slightly above $12.5 billion , to Chilean billionaire Jean Eric Salata. In March, Ross agreed to sell one percent of the team to Xiaomi co-founder Lin Bin at a valuation of $12.5 billion.

Besides the Dolphins , Salata now owns a piece of Hard Rock Stadium, the F1 Hard Rock Miami Grand Prix and the Miami Open tennis championships, which all now fall under Ross Sports & Entertainment.

The sale is expected to be approved by NFL owners at their meeting next week in New York. According to the Sports Business Journal, the league's finance committee approved the transaction last month.

According to SBJ, Salata, 60, is chairman of the Swedish investment firm EQT AB, which in 2022 acquired the private equity firm he founded in Hong Kong, Baring Private Equity Asia. He is worth $8.4 billion, according to Forbes.

Ross previously sold 10 percent of the Dolphins and his other sports properties to Ares Management and a combined 3 percent stake to Nets owner Joe Tsai and Nets minority owner Oliver Weisberg in December 2024. That came five months after NFL owners voted 31-1 to open the door to private equity groups.

In the latest Forbes 400 list, released last month, Ross ranked 56th with a value of $21.5 billion. Ross heads Related Companies, which has numerous real estate holdings in Palm Beach County.

The Dolphins are tied for 11th among NFL franchises , according to Forbes, valued at $7.5 billion, which also includes Hard Rock Stadium, the Miami Open and the Miami Grand Prix . The Dallas Cowboys top that list at $17 billion.

According to SBJ research, the average of all public estimates of the Dolphins' value, plus those other properties, is $10.59 billion .

In August, Ross named his son-in-law, Daniel Sillman , CEO and head of football operations.

articles.title: What's wrong with Marvin Harrison Jr. in the NFL and how the Texans can fix it
articles.summary: The Texans traded for the can't-miss 'Maserati' from Ohio State as a reclamation project. Did they get a Mazda instead?
articles.body:
Marvin Harrison Jr. greeted the media with a smile on Wednesday in new Houston Texans gear.

Blue headband. White sweatshirt. It's a change of scenery for the No. 4 pick in the 2024 NFL Draft. What excites Harrison most ahead of his debut on Sunday against the Jacksonville Jaguars at 9:30 a.m. ET at Wembley Stadium in London, England?

"It's just a combination of everything, really," Harrison said at his press conference . "I can't pinpoint one thing. I think the team as a whole. It's great for me. It's a great situation for me. Being with C.J. (Stroud) with a quarterback you have rapport with and had success with in the past is great, too."

That's the easy-to-see connection. The Arizona Cardinals traded Harrison — who did not live up to expectations as a top-five pick through two-plus seasons — to the Texans. Harrison is reunited with his old quarterback and the hope is to rekindle a connection from their time together at Ohio State.

Sirius XM NFL analyst Jacob Hester, host of "Movin' the Chains," said that relationship helps explain a second chance for Harrison with the Texans.

"It's always tough when you have high expectations and you don't live up to them and a lot of people are questioning why it didn't work," Hester told The Sporting News. "Was it you? Was it the team? What was it? Dealing with that is always tough. You never know if getting back with C.J. Stroud is going to be the thing that unlocks his career and he shows that potential we saw at Ohio State, but I can tell you it's going to make him more comfortable."

Marvin Harrison's place among Ohio State receivers

Steele Chambers played linebacker at Ohio State from 2019-23. He remembers a few occasions where he was lined up across from Harrison in practice.

"There were a couple times where I got stuck on him in the slot and it was next to impossible to stay with him on a route," Chambers told The Sporting News.

Harrison had back-to-back seasons with more than 1,200 receiving yards. He caught 14 TDs both years and finished fourth in the Heisman Trophy voting in 2023. Chambers saw the work ethic. Harrison was on the JUGS machine catching passes after practice "all the time."

Harrison is one of six first-round picks at receiver in that stretch along with Chris Olave (2021), Garrett Wilson (2021), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (2023), Emeka Egbuka (2025) and Carnell Tate (2026). Jeremiah Smith will be the next one in the 2027 NFL Draft and could be the No. 1 pick.

This is part of the reason for the surprise that Harrison hasn't taken off at the next level. As a freshman, Harrison caught three TDs in the 48-45 victory against No. 10 Utah in the Rose Bowl on Jan. 1, 2022 – and that foreshadowed a dominant two–year stretch with the Buckeyes in 2023-24.

"All these Ohio State receivers that have come out in recent years have something that makes them the best of the best," Chambers said. "Whenever I look at Jaxon Smith-Njigba, his big thing was he was very smooth in his route running. He was just able to get open in his 1-on-1s. Marvin Harrison, he runs pretty good routes, but his big thing was contested catches. He was making these catches in the corner of the end zone with a dude draped on top of him. Even though those are spectacular to watch, you're not seeing the separation that a JSN gets where he is just wide open running on defense."

Why did Marvin Harrison Jr. struggle with the Arizona Cardinals?

Given the track record of success from the Ohio State pipeline, Harrison seemed like a lock to have success when the Arizona Cardinals drafted him in 2024.

Harrison had 62 catches for 885 yards and eight TDs as a rookie in 2024, but that production slipped to 41 catches for 608 yards and four TDs. He was the third option behind tight end Trey McBride and receiver Michael Wilson.

Hester did not see this as an "Arizona problem." Harrison had two different quarterbacks in Kyler Murray and Jacoby Brissett, two different coaches in Jonathan Gannon and Mike LaFleur and two coordinators in Drew Petzing and Nathaniel Hackett.

"When I watched the tape, I was surprised that he wasn't able to make the plays that were there for him," Hester said. "What I mean by that is, if the coverage is here, this is the route that I run, I catch the football and get what the play gives me. He wasn't doing that."

Chambers said being the No. 1 receiver for the Buckeyes is, "Basically like being the dude for a NFL team. That's the way people view Ohio State football." Yet Harrison dealt with other expectations including his father, Marvin Harrison Sr., who is fifth all-time in receptions (1,102), fifth in TDs (128) and ninth in receiving yards (14,580) as a Hall of Fame receiver with the Indianapolis Colts from 1996-2008.

"I'm surprised how the last couple years have went," Chambers said. "I feel like his rookie year, everything was thinking he was going to eclipse 1,200 yards, 90 receptions. Now, he didn't do too bad. … He had a solid rookie year, and I feel like everybody thought he was going to take off and it didn't take off the way that you thought.

To Chambers' point about contested catches: Harrison was 29 of 63 (46%) the last three seasons in Arizona, which was a little less than 32 of 61 (52.5%) at Ohio State from 2021-23.

It culminated this season when Harrison was limited to five catches and 85 yards and a TD in four games before being traded to Houston.

"I think at some point he started pressing so much and he wasn't making those plays," Hester said. "It's hard to point to one reason, but there was definitely a disconnect in who he was as a player and what they were trying to do offensively. That's with multiple quarterbacks and multiple coordinators."

Will Marvin Harrison Jr. and C.J. Stroud work in Houston?

If it's about more opportunities, then Harrison should get those with Stroud in Houston.

"With CJ Stroud, now you have a dude in a system that can actually trust him to make those catches and can get him the football, then you start to see his skill actually show up," Chambers said. "In Arizona he wasn't getting those chances."

There also is a different role to play with the Texans. Nico Collins — who had three straight 1,000-yard seasons from 2023-25 — is the clear No. 1 receiver. That should work to Harrison's advantage.

"Marvin Harrison Jr. is going to have to be a complimentary piece, and that's OK," Hester said. "The thing about complimentary pieces, you've gotta be trusted. If I'm Marvin Harrison, like on third downs, you're going to know No. 18 is going to be open."

Chambers sees a similar outlook, where Harrison should be able to succeed in that role.

"He was pretty reserved, a guy that just kind of went about his business," Chambers said. "I don't know where he is mentally, but I do think a change of scenery and maybe going to a Texans' team where he's not forced to be a superstar right off the bat — like he's just another guy in the receiver room trying to pay his dues — I think that's going to go a long way for him."

Chambers remembers Stroud and Harrison being tight in college, and the early social media clips are leaning into that reunion. That's also an easy-to-see piece.

"You can play a long time in this league if he goes back to that," Hester said. "That was his best year. That was his most-productive year. So find that thing when you first get to Houston, make it your thing and then grow into the role after that."

For his part, Harrison kept it simple in that press conference. He is not concerned about what went wrong in Arizona or the notion of being labeled a first-round bust.

"Everybody has their own opinions. That's the best way I can put that … I know who I am as a player and who I am as a person."

He also knows why Houston traded for him.

articles.title: Chiefs-Chargers Week 6 game and score predictions from Arrowhead Pride
articles.summary: Putting our predictions on the record before Kansas City’s Sunday afternoon home game with Los Angeles.
articles.body:
It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs host the Los Angeles Chargers , our writers predicted the final score and result.

The Chargers may not have had the "Offseason Champions" accolades they frequently boast entering the season, but few expected an 0-5 start and making a case for the NFL's worst offense. They will try to get their first win on the road against a rested Chiefs squad coming off the bye. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists Kansas City as 8.5-point home favorites.

When last on the field, the Chiefs were tested but came out undefeated against the Las Vegas Raiders at Allegiant Stadium in Week 4.

We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction !

The Chargers' 0-5 start is perhaps the season's biggest development. Still, a division game should always be taken seriously.

Yes, it would be easier to name the Chargers not on this week's injury report than to speculate on who might play through a number of serious ailments. Yes, Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh appear to be from different planets. But I'm going to plan a close game.

Even if they play without longtime Travis Kelce nemesis Derwin James, I expect the Chargers defense to do what they've done for years: make this an ugly game that comes down to the fourth quarter. I expect Kansas City to come out on top, but I'm planning for a frustrating Sunday afternoon.

I did not expect this to be the season of the Chargers' undoing, but it has come at a good time for the Chiefs as they work their way back to the top of the AFC.

The Chargers swept the Chiefs last season for the first time in nearly a decade, and Mahomes tore his ACL in the game that led to the Chiefs being eliminated from playoff contention. Despite the lopsided record and multiple players out, I still expect both teams to come out with plenty of juice. The Chargers to save their season, but the Chiefs will remind them that the AFC West still runs through Arrowhead Stadium despite the results of last season. Andy Reid off of a Bye Week is always an advantage, and his team will enter the game at nearly full health. With multiple starters out, I expect the Chargers to try to play the clock and play keep-away from Mahomes to help keep themselves in the game. The Chiefs offense will be without their key deep threat, Tyquan Thornton, but the combination of Mahomes and Kenneth Walker should be enough to get past the floundering Chargers.

I don't see the Chiefs having much trouble taking care of business against the Chargers on Sunday. We already know Andy Reid's track record coming off a bye week, and now he's facing an 0-5 Chargers team that's absolutely decimated by injuries. On top of that, Justin Herbert is playing some of the worst football of his career. I expect the Chiefs to come out sharp, handle business, and win this one comfortably.

The Chargers enter Week 6 at 0-5, making them one of the NFL's biggest surprises for all the wrong reasons. Justin Herbert and the offense have struggled under new offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, although the defense has kept them competitive. Injuries along the offensive line only make things tougher against an undefeated Chiefs team coming off a bye. On paper, Kansas City should win comfortably. But a winless division rival fighting for its season makes this a dangerous matchup. The Chargers would love nothing more than to hand the Chiefs their first loss.

I don't see that happening Sunday. Despite injuries at wide receiver, Kansas City can continue leaning on Kenneth Walker III to keep the offense moving and create opportunities for Patrick Mahomes through play-action. Defensively, this feels like the week "Sack Nation" returns, with the Chiefs taking advantage of a depleted offensive line and making Herbert uncomfortable. Los Angeles will put up a fight, but Andy Reid's team will leave the bye ready to handle business.

Your 4-0 Kansas City Chiefs are back to face another division opponent after the bye week. The winless Los Angeles Chargers come to town as the most disappointing team in the league after being a favorite breakout team for approximately 30 straight offseasons. They aren't untalented but have played poorly. That makes them dangerous at 0-5 with their backs aga the wall. Expect a close, bitter contest between division rivals, regardless of the records. Herbert will probably throw a couple of touchdowns, especially if his top 2WRs were back in the lineup. It's all going to come down to how well the Chiefs can execute. I expect the pass rush will get 3+ sacks. I expect Walker to have 100 total yards. I don't know what to expect from the Chiefs receivers. Will Cyrus Allen get a real shot? Will Xavier Worthy produce? Can they make up for injuries to Rice and Thornton? My prediction is that it won't be pretty, but it will be enough.

Throw the records out for this one. To me, it doesn't matter the Chiefs are undefeated and the Chargers are winless. Every time these teams play, it seems to be a battle that comes down to the wire. And despite being winless and at times inept, the last three losses for the Chargers have all been by a score.

These teams know each other, and I think it will be another close game. I don't expect a full game from Rashee Rice if he does play, and this leaves the receiver room as a major question mark. Expect a big game from Travis Kelce and for the pass rush to finally get home multiple times against the Chargers' beat up offensive line.

Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh is a franchise vampire. He drains the talent out of an organization and gets as many wins as he can before they shrivel up into a corpse. Unfortunately, the Chargers were already halfway to hospice by the time he took the reins.

In the end, Ol' Khaki Bottle Glasses will pin the Chargers 30th-ranked offense on offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel (AKA The Vape Prince) to buy himself another year. But how is the Chargers 22nd ranked defense Captain E-Cig's fault?

The Chiefs are coming out of the bye. Despite being banged up at wide receiver, as long as they don't play down to the competition, they should take care of business.

Chiefs-Chargers has been exciting for the past couple of years and had a lot of intrigue coming into the season. That is no longer the case, as the Chargers are 0-5 and a complete train wreck. There's a good chance the Chargers' entire staff gets fired. They're incredibly banged up on offense, and the whole unit seems checked out. Division games can get weird, but with the Chiefs off a bye and the Chargers facing this opponent, I feel like they should easily cruise to a win.

When a team is in as much of a down spell as the Chargers are, the Chiefs have no excuse to let them up off the ground. Los Angeles' incredible injury report, which named more than 20 players on Thursday, reflects how broken the team has looked over five games. Quarterback Justin Herbert hasn't elevated the team with his own play, so it's on Kansas City to do what it takes to ensure he doesn't get a bounce-back performance.

That's what it will take to beat the Chiefs in Arrowhead on Sunday. Off a bye week, the team should relish this opportunity at home and take care of business. Expect defensive tackle Chris Jones to come off a bye week and lead a resurgent pass rush, taking advantage of strong man coverage on the back end to tally multiple sacks on Herbert in an imperfect victory that moves the team to 5-0.

The AP panel was split in Week 4 between predicting a comfortable or a close victory for Kansas City . All nine staffers on the panel did correctly predict the Chiefs would win. Jared Sapp (34-31) and Ron Kopp Jr. (23-20) did predict three-point margins. Jared tied with Matt Stagner's 31-24 prediction to lead the way with only eight points of error. Matt has been the panel's overall most accurate member through the season's quarter mark.

92.4% of our readers predicted a Chiefs victory , with 60 .3% anticipating a close score.

*To calculate a prediction's points of error, the differences between the prediction and the actual score in point spread, home team score, and away team score are added together. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Rankings: 5 most polarizing players for Week 6
articles.summary: Hayden Winks goes over the 5 most polarizing players for fantasy football among his rankings for Week 6.
articles.body:
We have five Yahoo rankers every week , and this column will look at five of the buzziest names of the week. I'm looking for players where there is real disagreement, and I'm using a little something called "coefficient of variation" to help me find just that. These rankings will be tinkered all the way until kickoff, so please check back in on our weekly rankings pages and Sunday AM sit/start show for the absolute latest.

These blurbs are also in The Blueprint, which is my weekly rankings and analysis column. The RB version is out on Wednesdays, while the WR version and the QB/TE/K/DEF version are each out on Thursdays before Thursday Night Football.

Marks set season highs in just about all categories last week after David Montgomery (groin) left. He was the RB23 on RB11 expected half PPR points (16.9), playing 56 of 57 snaps without Monty. If he plays nearly 100% of the snaps in the interim, Marks has an RB2 profile. The Texans' RB room has averaged 17.9 expected half PPR points this season for reference. Marks' tape has been better than Montgomery's, too, largely because the difference in juice is pretty staggering on top of Marks' comfort as a checkdown and screen player.

This week brings a matchup with the Jaguars, who rank third-best in half PPR points allowed (13.4 per game) to opposing backfields. They've allowed the fewest points on runs to RBs but have allowed 6.8 half PPR points through the air to them, including 11 receptions from Chase Brown in Week 4. Marks will need them to pay off because there's just no way this OL is ready for this DL. Houston enters the road contest with an implied team total of 19.75 points (22nd) as 3.0-point underdogs.

After Kaleb Johnson fumbled late in Week 4 and Chris Brooks went to IR, it's been almost entirely Lloyd. The Packers mixed in Pierre Strong Jr. in protection, but Lloyd handled 10 carries in a bombs-away Packers game plan. He finished with a truck-stick TD and an untouched TD in the red zone. His 13.1 and 10.0 expected half PPR points over the past two weeks are enough to "trust" Lloyd as a fringe fantasy RB2, while the Packers and everyone else await the NFL's decision on Josh Jacobs. Lloyd is still very unreliable on film, so he's still treated as a very boom-bust option.

The Packers get a Cowboys defense that is seventh in half PPR points allowed to opposing RBs this season at 23.6 points per game. Dallas was just gashed by Bucky Irving for 165 rushing yards and 30.5 half PPR points in Week 5, while Derrick Henry managed 21.4 points against them in Week 3. Green Bay is a 1.5-point home favorite with an implied team total of 27 points (fourth). The starting RB on a team projected that well simply needs to be in lineups.

We'll see if Saquon Barkley can return, but if not, Pierce is the next man's next man's next man up. Pierce handled every RB opportunity after Will Shipley's foot injury, and he's only up against meme'd RB/FB Carson Steele and meme'd LV-wearing RB Jaydon Blue for touches. Those touches won't go anywhere behind three backups along the OL and some of the worst TE/WR blocking in the NFL, but at least we can pretend they will until the game starts.

The Panthers have real talent up front at DT, EDGE and LB when fully healthy, so I wouldn't buy into the fact that they've allowed the third-most fantasy points to RBs this season on the second-most rushing yards. They've at least slowed down Jahmyr Gibbs (77 total yards) and Bijan Robinson (81 scoreless total yards) since that wild game to the Bears. Philadelphia has a 21.5-point team total (18th).

Egbuka is the Bucs' best pass-catcher by far, and the offense does build their go-to plays through him on tape. He's in motion often and should have better days when the QB play cooperates. Egbuka is not the most explosive player, but he can be a Jakobi Meyers presence at the very worst, with better skills for a flanker/slot role than as a downfield X receiver. He is playing inside more often this year with Ted Hurst taking on the vertical role, but it's asking a lot for an undrafted rookie QB to make these throws. Egbuka has been the WR66 and WR7 in expected points with Jalon Daniels under center, and that sums up the unpredictability of the situation. Egbuka is the WR32 on WR28 usage, smoothing out the entire season.

Pittsburgh represents a stingy test through the air, ranking 27th in WR half PPR points allowed at 22.3 per game. While Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins each topped 90 receiving yards and a touchdown against them in Week 3, the Colts and Browns failed to have a top-30 WR in recent games. This pass rush is intimidating, and the betting markets agree. Tampa Bay is a 3-point home underdog with an implied team total of 18.75 points (24th).

Fannin doesn't have a single screen target this season after being one of the best YAC weapons last year. The Browns are getting the ball to KC Concepcion, who was cleared to play in Week 6, in the manufactured touch game, while also throwing it downfield more often. He looked banged up on a few of his reps last week to me. Fannin is still the TE10 on TE11 usage this month, but the floor is lower this year, even without David Njoku. His 0.92 yards per route are nearly half of last year's 1.64.

This week brings a home matchup against a Ravens defense that ranks 18th in half PPR scoring allowed to TEs but has superstar SCB/SS Kyle Hamilton to roam in the Fannin waters. A team total of just 18.0 points (27th) works against Fannin's TE1 odds.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Troy Aikman's Dolphins Role Amid Questions Around 'Monday Night Football' Future
articles.summary: Hall of Fame quarterback and ESPN color commentator Troy Aikman doesn't currently have a role with the Miami Dolphins as his future on the Monday Night Football broadcast is up in the air, according to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.
articles.body:
Hall of Fame quarterback and ESPN color commentator Troy Aikman doesn't currently have a role with the Miami Dolphins as his future on the Monday Night Football broadcast is up in the air, according to Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.

Per Maske, Aikman has no "formal and ongoing agreement" to be a Dolphins consultant after previously operating in the role on a temporary basis during the 2026 offseason.

Aikman is in the final year of a five-year deal with ESPN that pays him $18 million per season, via Dan Shanoff of The Athletic.

Front Office Sports' Ryan Glasspiegel also reported that there has been "tension" between Aikman and longtime broadcast partner Joe Buck, who reportedly received a new contract from ESPN.

Aikman addressed his relationship with Buck during a Thursday appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas (via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News ).

"There's probably a time and a place for all that. I don't know if now is the time," Aikman said. "I don't know if it's hard to figure out kind of what happened. I'll broadcast through this season and I'll be a free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens. I'm looking forward to whatever the rest of this season does hold and the Super Bowl and all that and where my next landing spot may be."

Aikman could end up joining a new network once the 2026 season comes to a close, although it's worth noting that he faced restrictions in the lead-up to Monday Night Football broadcasts this year due to his role with the Dolphins.

He's required to remotely attend production meetings and is not permitted to attend practices at team facilities, per ESPN .

Maske noted Friday that Aikman's official consulting role in Miami was limited to the team's searches for a new head coach and general manager. Jeff Hafley and Jon-Eric Sullivan were eventually hired for the respective positions.

articles.title: Packers' Josh Jacobs to Be Removed From NFL Exempt List, Will Be Eligible for Week 7 vs. Lions
articles.summary: The NFL announced Friday that it is removing Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner Exempt List, making him eligible to play in the team's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25.
articles.body:
The NFL announced Friday that it is removing Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs from the Commissioner Exempt List, making him eligible to play in the team's Week 7 game against the Detroit Lions on Oct. 25.

Jacobs' attorneys released the following statement on his behalf:

On Sunday, Jacobs will miss his sixth game of the season since being placed on the commissioner exempt list on Aug. 30.

The league made the decision to place Jacobs on the commissioner exempt list days after he was charged with misdemeanor battery and criminal damage stemming from a May dispute with his then-girlfriend.

Jacobs pleaded no contest to the charges last month, and he was ordered to pay a $1,000 fine.

As part of an agreement with prosecutors, the criminal damage charge can be dismissed in a year if Jacobs "fulfills terms that include staying out of trouble, avoiding the victim in this case, submitting to supervision, completing counseling and paying restitution to the victim."

Jacobs was arrested on May 26 after his then-girlfriend told police that he had thrown her to the ground and taken her phone.

Police noticed redness on her face and neck, and a bump on her head. They also viewed surveillance video that corroborated the woman's story.

The 28-year-old Jacobs is a seven-year NFL veteran who has played for the Las Vegas Raiders and Packers.

Originally selected 24th overall by the Raiders in the 2019 NFL draft, Jacobs is a three-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro who has rushed for 7,803 yards and 74 touchdowns, while catching 269 passes for 2,072 yards and two scores over 105 career regular-season games.

Last season, Jacobs finished with 929 yards and 13 touchdowns on the ground, plus 36 receptions for 282 yards and one touchdown in 15 games.

The 3-2 Packers have struggled mightily to run the ball so far this season without Jacobs, ranking last in the NFL in rushing yards per game (60.4), and 31st in yards per carry (3.1).

articles.title: Jalen Hurts' Health Discussed by Eagles HC Nick Sirianni, Devonta Smith, More
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss his team's home game on Sunday vs. the Carolina Panthers as he deals with a superficial blood clot initially discovered last Saturday.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss his team's home game on Sunday vs. the Carolina Panthers as he deals with a superficial blood clot initially discovered last Saturday.

Both head coach Nick Sirianni and wide receiver Devonta Smith spoke about Hurts on Friday with reporters.

"I'm always concerned for our guys. Jalen and I have a special relationship. There's times I've said to Jalen, 'I know you like I know my brother,'" Sirianni said at his Friday press conference with reporters (h/t ESPN's Tim McManus ).

"We've spent a lot of time together. We've been to the highest of highs, we've had lows. ... Your first reaction is always the care for the player because this is not just a coach-player relationship."

Smith has this to say when asked if he spoke with Hurts.

"He's fine," Smith said. "It's bigger than football. Something like this that's very serious puts a lot of things into perspective."

The Eagles have gone 59-28 in Hurts' starts over seven seasons since he took over as QB 1 late in the 2020 season. Philadelphia has won a pair of NFC titles and a Super Bowl with Hurts at the helm.

This year has been a struggle for Hurts and the 2-3 Eagles, who are fourth-last in scoring (18.4 PPG). Hurts has completed 57.8 percent of his passes for 933 yards (6.1 yards per attempt) and eight touchdowns (three interceptions). He's also rushed for 107 yards and another score.

Hopefully Hurts will be back as soon as possible for Philadelphia. He's certainly dealing with a scary situation right now after news that the blood clot moved.

He certainly has the concern of his teammates, including wideout Dontayvion Wicks.

"It's hard when you find out your leader has to sit out for something like that," Wicks said, per McManus. "It's real serious. You never know what people are going through because he played the game last week and we didn't know. But we just stick by his side and be there for him while he's going through what he's going through and just doing what we've got to do until he gets back."

In the meantime, Tanner McKee will take over for the Eagles as QB1. He's attempted passes in four games over two seasons, completing 54-of-88 throws (61.4 percent) for 597 yards (6.8 yards per attempt), five touchdowns and one interception.
